label: JW · play
title: Jesus is the uncreated Creator (John 1:3 / Col 1:16)
text: "According to John 1:3, how many things came into existence without the Word?" (Answer: not one.)

label: JW · if they say
title: "'All' doesn't always mean all."
text: Here the verse defines it: "in the heavens and on the earth, visible and invisible, thrones, lordships" (Col 1:16). And John 1:3 says "not one thing."

label: JW · if they say
title: "He was Jehovah's master worker (Prov 8:30)."
text: Working alongside doesn't mean created. And Prov 8 personifies Wisdom (a "she"). Is God ever without wisdom?

label: JW · play
title: Jesus is Yahweh (the "First and Last" / Hebrews 1 chain)
text: "Who is the First and the Last in Isaiah 44:6?" (They'll say Jehovah.) "Does being the First and the Last mean you have a beginning?" (No.)

label: JW · if they say
title: "Jesus is the 'first and last' in a different sense."
text: "Then show me the text that makes the difference." Same title, same book, same speaker formula.

label: JW · if they say
title: "Hebrews 1:8 should say 'God is your throne.'"
text: v.8 opens "to the Son He says." The Father is speaking to the Son. And v.10 ("You, Lord…") has no throne issue at all.

label: JW · play
title: The Spirit is a Person and is Jehovah
text: "Does the Holy Spirit speak? Yes or no?" → Run the full 🔥 Holy Spirit Play. Best JW order: Acts 13:2 → Eph 4:30 → 2 Sam 23:2–3 + Acts 4:24–25. Witnesses often have no prepared answer at this point.

label: JW · play
title: Jesus is good, so He is God (Mark 10:18)
text: "Is Jesus good?" (They'll hesitate.)

label: JW · if they say
title: "He's not good like God"
text: "Name the moral flaw Jesus has that the Father doesn't."

label: JW · play
title: Watchtower prophecy test (use when they lean on the organization)
text: "Has the Watchtower ever announced a date in Jehovah's name that didn't happen?" "Have you heard of Beth Sarim, the mansion the Watchtower built in San Diego in 1929? Do you know who it was built for?"

label: JW · if they say
title: "We're not prophets, just students making calculations"
text: "Announcing future dates as God's truth is prophecy by definition."

label: JW · play
title: Only God can pay the ransom (Psalm 49)
text: "According to Psalm 49:7, can any man redeem his brother or give God a ransom for him?" (They'll say no.) This is a cumulative case. Psalm 49 does not name Jesus, and it does not prove the Trinity on its own. It says no mere man can pay the ransom and that God will redeem. The New Testament then says Jesus paid it, and calls Him God.

label: JW · if they say
title: "Psalm 49 is about imperfect men. Jesus was a perfect man, a corresponding ransom for Adam."
text: The psalm makes no exception for a perfect man. Its answer is "God will redeem." And every creature worships the Lamb for the people He purchased (Rev 5:9; Rev 5:13–14). "Would Jehovah share that worship with a creature?" (Isa 42:8)

label: JW · if they say
title: "Jehovah provided the ransom. Jesus was only the price."
text: Yes, the Father sent the Son. But the One who gave Himself is called our great God and Savior (Titus 2:13–14).

label: JW · if they say
title: "Acts 20:28 should read 'the blood of His own Son.'"
text: That verse speaks of God purchasing the church with blood. Some manuscripts read "church of the Lord," and some translations say "the blood of His own." Don't rest the case on this one verse; the chain above stands without it.

label: JW · objection
title: "John 1:1 says 'a god.' No article = indefinite."
text: A predicate noun before the verb without the article describes nature (Harner: qualitative). "The Word was God" in nature: all that God is, the Word was. "Is God 'a love'? Was John sent from 'a god'? Your NWT says 'God' in 1:6. Why not in 1:1?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Ton theon = the Almighty; theos = a lesser god."
text: That's just Greek case. Ton theon is accusative after pros; theos is nominative. Case endings aren't ranks. "Is the Father a lesser god when he's in the nominative?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Firstborn of creation" (Col 1:15) = first created
text: Prōtotokos = preeminent heir. v.16 gives the reason: "because by Him all things were created." "Who was Israel's first king? Saul. So how is David 'firstborn' of the kings?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Only-begotten" (John 3:16) = uniquely created
text: Monogenēs = the unique, only begotten Son, never "created" (Heb 11:17: Isaac wasn't Abraham's only son). "Was Isaac Abraham's only child?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Beginning of the creation of God" (Rev 3:14)
text: Archē = origin / ruler / source. He's where creation comes from. "If you're the originator of your business, aren't you its origin?"

label: JW · objection
title: "John 5:19: Jesus can do nothing on his own"
text: That shows the Persons are distinct and act together. Finish the verse: "whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise." "Does the Father do anything without the Son?"

label: JW · objection
title: "John 14:28: 'the Father is greater than I'"
text: Greater in role, in the Son's humbled human state. Not in nature. Phil 2:6–7. "Is a husband 'greater' in nature than his wife because he leads?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Psalm 8 / Heb 2: everything is subject to man, not Jesus"
text: Heb 2:9 identifies the "him": "namely Jesus." "Who are we going to trust, you or the author of Hebrews?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Daniel 7: Jesus wasn't seated / Rev 3:21: believers sit on the throne too"
text: Sharing kingdom authority ≠ sitting on high in heaven, the place that belongs to Yahweh alone (Ps 113:5). "Show me anyone other than Jesus who sits 'on high' at the right hand of the Majesty."

label: JW · objection
title: "Holy Spirit = active force"
text: → 🔥 Holy Spirit Play "Can a force be grieved?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Trinity isn't in the Bible."
text: Word–concept fallacy. "Jehovah's Witness" isn't in the Bible as a denomination name either. Is the concept taught? "Is the word 'theocracy' in the Bible?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus is Michael the Archangel."
text: Scripture never says it. Michael did not dare rebuke Satan himself (Jude 9); Jesus commands him directly (Matt 4:10). God never called any angel "My Son," and all the angels worship the Son. "To which of the angels did God ever say, 'You are My Son'?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus was raised as a spirit, not in a body."
text: He said a spirit does not have flesh and bones as He has, He showed His wounds, and He said He would raise His body. "In John 2:19–21, what did Jesus say He would raise?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Only 144,000 go to heaven."
text: Right after the 144,000, John sees a great multitude no one could count standing before the throne, serving God in His temple. "Where is the great multitude standing in Rev 7:9?"

label: JW · objection
title: "The dead are unconscious. The soul stops existing."
text: Paul expected to depart and be with Christ, away from the body and at home with the Lord. The souls under the altar speak. "How do the souls in Rev 6:10 cry out if they don't exist?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Hell isn't eternal. The wicked are simply destroyed."
text: Jesus uses the same word, "eternal," for the punishment and for the life in one sentence. "If the punishment isn't eternal, is the life?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus died on a stake, not a cross."
text: Don't make this the fight. Thomas speaks of nails, plural, in His hands, and the sign was placed above His head. Then go back to who Jesus is. "Why 'nails,' plural, for His hands?"

label: JW · objection
title: "You must use God's name, Jehovah."
text: The apostles take the Old Testament "name" texts and apply them to Jesus. Joel's "call on the name of Yahweh" becomes confessing Jesus as Lord. "In Rom 10:13, whose name is in view, given verse 9?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus is a god, a mighty one, but not the true God."
text: Jehovah says no god was formed before or after Him and He knows of no other. So is Jesus a true God or a false god? Thomas calls Him "my Lord and my God" and Jesus accepts it. "Is Jesus a true god or a false god?"

label: JW · objection
title: "People only did obeisance to Jesus, not worship."
text: All the angels worship the Son. Every creature gives the same honor to God and to the Lamb. An angel refuses it; Jesus receives it. "Why does the angel refuse what Jesus accepts?"

label: JW · objection
title: "You need Jehovah's organization to be saved."
text: Salvation is by grace through faith, not works, and not membership. When others left, Peter did not ask where to go, but to whom. "To whom did Peter say we should go?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus was a perfect man, a corresponding ransom for Adam. He didn't need to be God."
text: He had to be truly man to die in our place. But Scripture says no man can ransom another, and that God Himself redeems. The One who paid is the Word, who was God and became flesh. Run Only God can pay the ransom. "Psalm 49 says no man can pay it. So what kind of man is Jesus?"

label: JW · quick card
title: John 1:3: "not one thing came into existence without Him" → "So did Jesus create Himself?"

label: JW · quick card
title: Col 1:16–17 (NWT): "all other things." The word "other" isn't in the Greek, and the Watchtower's own interlinear shows it.

label: JW · quick card
title: Isa 44:6 + Rev 1:17 / 22:13: First and Last → "Does being the First and Last mean you have a beginning?"

title: Heb 1:10–12 + Ps 102:25–27: the Father addresses the Son with a Psalm spoken to Jehovah as Creator.

title: Acts 13:2 + Heb 3:7–11: the Spirit says "me / I," and the Spirit is the one tested in the wilderness → see 🔥 Holy Spirit Play.

label: JW · quick card
title: Deut 18:21–22: the 1914 / 1925 predictions → the test of a prophet.

label: Unitarian · play
title: The Holy Spirit (lead with this)
text: "Does the Spirit have a mind? Yes or no?" → 🔥 Holy Spirit Play. Best order against Unitarians: "Does the Spirit have a mind? Yes or no?" → Acts 13:2 → Heb 3:7–11 → 2 Sam 23:2–3 / Acts 4:25 → Rom 8:9 ("Spirit of Christ").

label: Unitarian · play
title: The Angel of Yahweh claims to be God, with no "thus says the Lord"
text: "Can we be honest with the text: does the Angel of God claim to be the God of Bethel? Yes or no?"

label: Unitarian · if they say
title: "Agency: a messenger speaks in the first person for the king."
text: "Show me the 'thus says the Lord.'" There isn't one. "Without it, how do you know when a messenger is speaking for God or for himself?" Moses talking in his tent and Jonah running away weren't oracles just because they had the "messenger" title.

label: Unitarian · if they say
title: "Can't an ambassador speak as the king?"
text: Use their analogy: "Can the agent of the King claim to BE the King?" "Yahweh can send agents, but agents can't claim to be Yahweh, or they drop dead."

label: Unitarian · if they say
title: "Malak means a lesser being, sent by a superior."
text: Malak / angelos names a function, not a nature. John the Baptist and his disciples are called angelos (Mark 1:2; Luke 7:24). "Does the word itself tell you what kind of being the messenger is?" "If I send you with a message, am I superior to you in nature?"

label: Unitarian · play
title: Christ is the Yahweh of the Exodus (1 Cor 8:6 → 10:9)
text: "Who's the one Lord in 1 Corinthians 8?" (They'll say Jesus.) "In Numbers 21, who did Israel test, and who sent the serpents?" (They'll say Yahweh.)

label: Unitarian · if they say
title: "Textual variant: some manuscripts say 'the Lord'"
text: Fine. In this same letter, the "one Lord" is Jesus Christ (8:6). Either reading lands in the same place.

label: Unitarian · play
title: Real pre-existence (John 1:3, Col 1:16, Heb 1)
text: "Do you believe that the Word was created?" (They'll say yes. Then go to John 1:3.) "According to John 1:3, was anything made without the Word? Yes or no?" "Who is the author of life according to Acts 3:15?"

label: Unitarian · play
title: The Messiah shares Yahweh's nature (Zech 13:7)
text: "In Zechariah 13:7, who is the Shepherd that gets struck?" (Jesus says it's Him, Matt 26:31.)

label: Unitarian · objection
title: The syllogism: "YHWH is the Most High; Jesus is the Son of the Most High; if Jesus is YHWH, Jesus is his own Father."
text: Equivocation. You're treating "Yahweh" as naming only one person. Scripture applies the name to the Father, the Son and the Spirit. Jesus is Yahweh, and He is not the person of the Father. "Is 'Judah' a person or a tribe?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "John 17:3: the Father is 'the only true God'"
text: Yes, the Father is the only true God. Trinitarians agree. "Only" excludes false gods, not the Son: the same John calls Jesus "the true God" (1 John 5:20). "Jude calls Jesus our 'only Lord.' Does that make the Father not Lord?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "1 Cor 8:6: one God, the Father"
text: Same verse: "one Lord, Jesus Christ." Paul splits the Shema (Deut 6:4) between Father and Son. If "one God, the Father" excludes Jesus from being God, "one Lord, Jesus" excludes the Father from being Lord. "Is the Father not Lord?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "God is not a man" (Num 23:19; Hos 11:9)
text: God is not a man by nature (who lies or changes). The Son took on a human nature (John 1:14) and stayed God. "Can the God who made human nature add it to Himself?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Jesus died, and God can't die"
text: The Person of the Son died in His human nature. The divine nature doesn't die. Two natures, one Person. "Who was crucified in 1 Cor 2:8?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Homoousios / Nicaea / the church invented it"
text: The term is a summary of biblical teaching, not new revelation. Answer from the text, not from church history. "Fine. Set Nicaea aside. Let's just read Rev 3:14 / John 1:3."

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Archē (Rev 3:14) = first creature" / "Abba means source"
text: Archē = origin / ruler / active cause. The NT is Greek, not Hebrew, and Abba means "Father." "Does the software exist before you made it?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Context limits 'Author of life' / 'all things'"
text: Make them show the verse that limits it. "Where in the chapter does it say that?" (then wait)

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "The Spirit is rational energy / information / a vibe"
text: → 🔥 Holy Spirit Play "Can energy be rational without personhood?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Jesus has a God (John 20:17), so He isn't God."
text: As true man He has a God. The same chapter has Thomas call Him "my God," and Hebrews calls the Son "God" while speaking of "Your God." Both are true of the one Person. "In Heb 1:8–9, who is called God, and who is His God?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Jesus didn't know the day or the hour (Mark 13:32)."
text: Two natures. As man He grew in wisdom; as God He knows all things. "How can Peter say, 'Lord, You know all things'?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "God cannot be tempted (James 1:13), but Jesus was."
text: He was tempted as man, from outside, and never sinned. That is the point of the incarnation: a true human High Priest. "Did the temptation ever find sin in Him?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "No one has ever seen God, but people saw Jesus."
text: Finish the verse: the only begotten God has explained Him. No one has seen the Father apart from the Son. And Isaiah saw Yahweh, and John says he saw Christ's glory. "Who did Isaiah see in the temple?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Philippians 2 only says Jesus didn't grasp at being equal with God."
text: He was existing in the form of God and then took the form of a slave. You cannot take on humanity if you were only ever human. "When did He 'take' the form of a slave, if He was only ever a man?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "The 'Word' in John 1 is God's plan, not a person."
text: The Word is with God, makes all things, becomes flesh, and shares glory with the Father before the world existed. Plans don't do that. "Can a plan share glory with the Father before the world existed?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "'Before Abraham was, I am' just means He was foreordained."
text: His hearers understood Him. They picked up stones. Nobody is stoned for being part of God's plan. "Why did they try to stone Him?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Thomas was only exclaiming in surprise (John 20:28)."
text: The text says Thomas said it to Him, and Jesus blesses the confession instead of rebuking it. "Does Jesus correct Thomas or commend him?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Jesus is called 'god' the way judges and Moses were."
text: No judge is worshiped by angels, called Creator, or called the true God. And all are to honor the Son just as they honor the Father. "Is anyone told to honor Moses just as they honor the Father?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Matthew 28:19 was added later."
text: Every Greek manuscript that contains the passage has the three-fold name, and Paul blesses in the same three-fold way. "Which manuscript leaves it out?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "There is one mediator, 'the man Christ Jesus' (1 Tim 2:5). A sinless man was enough."
text: He is truly man; a mediator for men must be. But the next verse says He gave Himself as a ransom, and Scripture says no man can ransom another: God redeems. Hebrews says He partook of flesh and blood, and you cannot take on what you already only are. A mediator between God and men stands on both sides. "Hebrews 2:14 says He partook of flesh and blood. Who was He before He did?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: Acts 13:2 → "Do actions have authority, or do persons?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: Heb 3:7–11 / Ps 95 → "Who's the 'Me' the Spirit says they tested?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: Gen 31:11–13 → the Angel of God says "I am the God of Bethel." "Where's the 'thus says the Lord'?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: 1 Cor 8:6 + 1 Cor 10:9 + Num 21:5–6 → "When was Christ put to the test with serpents?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: John 1:3 / Col 1:16 → "How were all things created through Him if He didn't exist yet?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: Isa 44:6 + Rev 1:17 → "So Yahweh has a beginning?"

label: Mormon · play
title: No gods before Him, no gods after Him (against exaltation)
text: "Can I read you something God says about Himself and get your take?"

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "1 Cor 15:40–41: celestial / terrestrial glories."
text: In context that's about kinds of resurrection bodies, compared to the sun, moon and stars. It's about glorified bodies, not becoming creator gods.

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "We're joint heirs with Christ (Rom 8:17)."
text: Yes, we inherit the kingdom. Inheriting the kingdom isn't becoming God.

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "We'll be like Him (1 John 3:2)."
text: Conformed to Christ's moral image with a glorified body. Not divine in nature.

label: Mormon · play
title: God has always been God (against "God was once a man")
text: "Can we agree that God in His nature has to be infinite, always existing?" (They'll say yes.) "Joseph Smith taught God was not always God, but became God. Is that hearsay or fact?" (Use when they bring up exaltation themselves.)

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "That's not official doctrine / just my thought"
text: King Follett discourse (Joseph Smith, 1844), "God himself was once as we are now." Then: "Whether it's official or not, if a teaching contradicts the eternal God, it's a false teaching."

label: Mormon · play
title: Three separate gods vs. one God (the "Godhead")
text: "So these are three separate gods, then?"

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "Jesus' baptism shows three separate beings."
text: It shows three distinct Persons. Distinct ≠ separate gods. One Being, three Persons.

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "Yahweh is the title of the Godhead council, like three judges sharing one court."
text: "If one judge steps out and says 'I am the court,' is that right?" But each Person is fully Yahweh, not a third of a committee. And Neh 9:6 says Yahweh alone created.

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "The Angel / Son is Yahweh only by agency."
text: "Can the agent of the King claim to be the King?"

label: Mormon · play
title: Phantom prophecy (Joseph Smith wrote himself into Genesis)
text: "Where can I read the prophecy about Joseph Smith in a text that Joseph Smith didn't produce?" "Why would God pick that person to re-reveal that prophecy?" (After you name JST Genesis 50:33 and 2 Nephi 3:15.)

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "Jesus read Himself into Isaiah too (Luke 4:21)"
text: "He's quoting a different prophet, from a public scroll. He didn't add new verses to Genesis."

label: Mormon · objection
title: "There was a Great Apostasy, so God restored the church through Joseph Smith."
text: Jesus promised the gates of hell would not prevail and that He'd be with His church always. "Did Jesus fail to keep His promise for 1,700 years?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Pray about the Book of Mormon and you'll feel a burning in the bosom."
text: Feelings test nothing. Scripture tells us to test by Scripture. The heart is deceitful. "If a Muslim feels a burning about the Quran, is it true too?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Ye are gods" (Ps 82:6 / John 10:34)
text: Ps 82 is about unjust human judges who "will die like men" (v.7). It's irony and judgment, not a promise of exaltation. "Do these 'gods' die?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "The Father has a body of flesh and bone."
text: God is spirit, invisible, and fills heaven and earth. "Does a spirit have flesh and bones?" (Luke 24:39)

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Ezekiel 37's two sticks = Bible + Book of Mormon."
text: Read v.15–22: the sticks are Judah and Joseph/Ephraim, the divided kingdoms joined into one nation under one king. "What does v.22 say the two sticks become?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Jesus is 'a god'; the Father is 'the God.'"
text: Scripture never calls Jesus "a god." He is the God: Titus 2:13, John 20:28. "Show me 'a god' in John 1:1."

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Baptism for the dead" (1 Cor 15:29)
text: Paul says "they" (some group), not "we." It's an ad hominem for the resurrection, not a command. Heb 9:27. "Where is it ever commanded?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "We are saved by grace after all we can do (2 Nephi 25:23)."
text: Scripture says grace through faith, not of works. God justifies the one who does not work but believes. Good works are the fruit, not the price. "Have you done all you can do?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "The Bible is true only as far as it is translated correctly. Plain and precious things were lost."
text: God promised His word would stand forever. We have manuscripts more than a thousand years older than Joseph Smith, and none of them contain the "lost" material he added. "Which verse was lost, and which manuscript shows it?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "We have a living prophet today."
text: In these last days God has spoken in His Son. Any prophet is tested by Scripture, and a different gospel is rejected even from an angel. "What happens to a prophet whose word contradicts Scripture?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Jesus and Lucifer are spirit brothers."
text: Jesus created all things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, including every angelic power. The Creator is not the brother of His creature. "If Jesus made everything invisible in heaven, who made Lucifer?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "We all lived as spirits with God before we were born."
text: God forms the spirit of man within him. Only Christ is "from above." "Who does Jesus say is from above, and who is from below?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "The priesthood was restored through Joseph Smith."
text: The Aaronic priesthood was set aside, and Jesus holds His priesthood permanently. Every believer is already part of a royal priesthood. "If Jesus holds it permanently, who else needs to?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Families are forever through temple marriage."
text: Jesus says that in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage. The temple veil was torn, and God does not dwell in temples made with hands. "What did Jesus say about marriage in the resurrection?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "There are three degrees of glory. Almost everyone is saved somewhere."
text: Jesus speaks of two roads and two ends: eternal punishment or eternal life. "How many destinations does Jesus name?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "We're Christians too. We believe in Jesus."
text: Be gentle here. Paul warns of "another Jesus." The question is which Jesus: the eternal God who made all things, or a created spirit who became a god. "Is the Jesus you trust the eternal Creator, or a being who became a god?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "James 1:5: ask God, and He will tell you it's true."
text: James is about wisdom in trials, not a test for new scripture. The Bereans were praised for checking everything against the Scriptures. "What did the Bereans check Paul against?"

label: Muslim · play
title: THE ISLAMIC DILEMMA (run it in phases)
text: "Does the Quran say the Torah and the Gospel came from Allah? Yes or no?" The Quran says the Torah and Gospel in Christians' and Jews' hands in the 7th century were God's word and confirmed them. We have the 7th-century Bible (and far older manuscripts: Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Dead Sea Scrolls). That Bible says Jesus is the Son of God, died and rose. Either the Bible is reliable, and it contradicts the Quran → Islam is false. Or the Bible is corrupted, and then the Quran confirmed a corrupted book → Islam is false. Either way, Islam fails.

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "It only confirms the original revelation, not what they had."
text: "Read it again: 'that which is with you.' Is there any part of the verse that says it's only confirming part, some, or a piece?"

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "It's general confirmation. It retells the stories and edits out the errors."
text: "Define 'confirm.'" (= verify as true). Then Q 2:85: "Does Allah allow people to believe some of the Scripture and reject the rest?" "Give me one verse that says the Quran only confirms part."

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "Q 2:79: woe to those who write the book with their own hands."
text: That condemns people making counterfeit books. It doesn't say the real Scripture was changed. "If I wrote a book with my own hands and said it's from God, does that mean the Quran is now corrupted?"

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "Q 5:13: they distort words from their places."
text: Distorting meaning / misquoting ≠ the text is lost. The same chapter tells them to judge by what they have (5:43, 47). And Q 6:115: "None can change His words."

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "Having it is like having $100. You can still lose it."
text: The texts are present tense: they literally brought out the scroll.

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "The Bible is corrupted" (said only after a verse goes against them)
text: "You brought me the Bible as a source to prove Muhammad. When we read it, it's suddenly corrupted?"

label: Muslim · if they say
title: They pivot to "Is Jesus God?" or "the Trinity is 3 gods."
text: "You're not going to 'is Jesus God' your way out of this. Defend the Quran first."

label: Muslim · play
title: Muhammad isn't in the Bible (the John 14 and Q 61:6 claims)
text: "So where does Jesus mention Muhammad?" "So the Comforter here, you believe that's Muhammad?" (Once they cite John 14.)

label: Muslim · play
title: Only God gives eternal life
text: "Who gives eternal life?" (God.)

label: Muslim · play
title: Son vs. servant
text: "Is Jesus the son of Allah?" (They'll say no.) "Where in the Bible does it say the Son of God is just a servant?" (When they say "son" only means servant.)

label: Muslim · play
title: Tawhid consistency (the Black Stone)
text: "Can the Black Stone benefit you or harm you? Yes or no?" "Why are people rubbing oil on this rock that doesn't do anything for you?"

label: Muslim · play
title: Moral problems (only if they claim Islam is morally superior)
text: "You say Islam is morally superior. Can we read a few verses of the Quran and see?" "It talks about the women that you're allowed to have, right?" (On Q 4:24.)

label: Muslim · objection
title: "How can God be 3 and 1?"
text: Three in one sense (Persons), one in another (Being). Different categories, no contradiction. "The Quran has several transmitted readings: Hafs, Warsh, Qalun. Is that three Qurans, or one?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus never said 'I am God, worship me.'"
text: He said things only God could say, and accepted what only God receives. Watch for the goalpost shift. "First you wanted a verse. Now it has to come from Jesus' mouth?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "God is not a man" (Hosea 11:9)
text: Correct by nature. The Son added a human nature. Two natures, one Person. And don't let them skip the verse you gave first. "Do you acknowledge Heb 1:3 says the Son is the exact imprint of God's nature?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Which God sent Jesus? Who was He praying to?"
text: One God, three Persons. The Father sent the Son. Jesus prayed as a true man. "In John 17:5 Jesus asks for the glory He had with the Father before the world existed. Can a mere prophet pray that?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus wasn't crucified" (Q 4:157)
text: Every early source, Christian and non-Christian (Josephus c. AD 93, Tacitus c. AD 116), agrees He was crucified. The Quran denies it 600 years later with no source. And the Injil the Quran confirms teaches it. "Who did Allah make look like Jesus, and did he deceive the disciples into starting Christianity?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Paul corrupted Jesus' message."
text: Paul's gospel was checked and approved by Peter, James and John. And Q 61:14 praises Jesus' disciples as Allah's helpers, who won. "Q 61:14 says Allah made Jesus' followers victorious. The faith that won taught what Paul taught. Did Allah back the wrong side?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Torah is one book, but you have five."
text: The Torah = Genesis to Deuteronomy, the five books of Moses: one Torah in five scrolls. Jewish tradition says Joshua added the account of Moses' death (Deut 34). "The Quran has 114 surahs. Is it 114 books, or one?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Trinity is pagan / Allah is 'the third of three'"
text: The Quran pictures worship of God, Jesus and Mary (Q 5:116; cf. Q 5:73–75). That is not the Trinity Christians believe: one God in three Persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit. "Which Christian ever taught Mary is part of the Trinity?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus ate, slept and prayed. God doesn't do that."
text: He is truly God and truly man. The Word became flesh. Hunger and sleep belong to His human nature; they don't cancel His divine nature. "If God chose to enter His creation as a man, who could stop Him?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Injil was one book given to Jesus. You have four, written by men."
text: "Gospel" means the good news about Jesus. And the Quran tells the people of the Gospel to judge by what they had in the 7th century, which was these four. "What Gospel did Christians have in Muhammad's day?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus was sent only to the lost sheep of Israel."
text: His earthly ministry went to Israel first, as promised. Then He sent His disciples to all nations, as Isaiah foretold. "Who does Jesus send them to in Matt 28:19?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Bible has contradictions and too many versions."
text: Translations are not different Bibles. The manuscript differences are known and printed in the footnotes, and no teaching depends on them. Ask for one and read it together. "Which contradiction? Let's read it."

label: Muslim · objection
title: "God can simply forgive. He doesn't need a sacrifice."
text: A judge who lets the guilty go is unjust. God will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. At the cross He is both just and the justifier. Even the Quran ransoms Abraham's son with a great sacrifice. "If a judge lets the guilty go free, is he a just judge?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "No one can carry another person's sins (Q 6:164)."
text: The Torah the Quran confirms is built on substitution: the sins of the people laid on another. Isaiah foretold One who would bear the iniquity of us all. And Jesus is not an unwilling bystander punished for a stranger. He is the Son who laid down His life of His own accord, as the Father purposed. "What does Isaiah 53:6 say Yahweh laid on Him?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Your own Bible says each person dies for his own sin (Deut 24:16; Ezek 18:20)."
text: Deuteronomy tells human courts not to execute a son for his father's crime. Ezekiel says God holds each person to account for his own sin. Both forbid punishing an unwilling innocent. Neither forbids a willing substitute whom God Himself appoints. The same Law commands the sacrifices, and Isaiah foretells the Servant who bears the sin of many. "If substitution is forbidden, what are the sacrifices in Leviticus for?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus was only a prophet. A prophet can't redeem anyone."
text: Agreed: no mere man can. The Psalms say no man can ransom his brother, and that God Himself will redeem. That is why the Redeemer had to be God become man. Jesus said He came to give His life as a ransom. "If no man can pay the ransom, who can?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus and His disciples were Muslims."
text: His disciples worshiped Him, called Him Lord and God, and preached that He was crucified and raised. "Would a Muslim say 'My Lord and my God' to Jesus?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Muhammad is named in Song of Songs 5:16."
text: The Hebrew word there is an ordinary word for "desirable," used by a bride about her beloved. The same word family describes Ezekiel's wife (Ezek 24:16) and Israel's children (Hos 9:16). "Is Muhammad also in Ezekiel 24:16, where the same word is used?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Islam is the fastest-growing religion, so it must be true."
text: Truth isn't a headcount. Jesus said the many take the wide road. "Is something true because many people believe it?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Quran is a miracle. No one can produce a chapter like it."
text: That test has no judge and no standard. The Quran gives a better test: check with those who read the Scripture before. "Who judges the contest, and by what standard?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus said, 'Why do you call Me good? Only God is good.'"
text: He didn't say He isn't good. He asked the man why he said it. Jesus calls Himself the Good Shepherd. "Is Jesus good?"

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 5:47: "Let the people of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein."

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 5:43: "How do they come to you for judgment while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah?"

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 2:41: "Believe in what I have sent down, confirming that which is with you."

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 2:85: "Do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part?"

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 6:115 / 18:27: "None can change His words."

label: Muslim · quick card
title: John 14:16–17: the Helper "dwells with you and will be in you." "Was Muhammad living with the disciples?"

label: Jewish · play
title: Who is Isaiah talking about? (the Servant of Isaiah 53)
text: "Would you read a passage from the prophet Isaiah with me and tell me who you think it describes?" "I'm a Christian because of the Hebrew Scriptures. Can I show you the chapter that did it?"

label: Jewish · if they say
title: "The servant is Israel."
text: Isaiah does call Israel God's servant (Isa 41:8), a servant he then calls blind and deaf (Isa 42:19). But in Isa 49:5–6 the Servant is the one who brings Jacob back and raises up the tribes of Israel. One restores the other. And this Servant is innocent (Isa 53:9), while Isaiah's Israel is "a people weighed down with iniquity" (Isa 1:4). "When did Israel suffer silently, willingly and sinlessly, to pay for someone else's sins?"

label: Jewish · if they say
title: "That is a Christian reading."
text: The Aramaic Targum, read in synagogues, renders Isa 52:13 "Behold, My servant the Messiah" [Targum Jonathan]. The Talmud gives Messiah a name from Isa 53:4 [Sanhedrin 98b]. Reading the servant as the nation became the standard answer with Rashi, in the eleventh century, a thousand years after Jesus. "Why did the reading change?"

label: Jewish · if they say
title: "We never read that in synagogue."
text: That is true. The weekly readings from the Prophets stop at Isa 52:12 and pick up again at Isa 54:1. Don't accuse anyone of hiding it. Just say, "Then let's read it now."

label: Jewish · if they say
title: "He was just a man who died. Many Jews were crucified."
text: Only one was foretold as dying for others' sins, buried in a rich man's tomb, and alive afterward. Go to The resurrection.

label: Jewish · play
title: Where is the atonement? (sin, sacrifice and no temple)
text: "On Yom Kippur, how do you know your sins are actually forgiven?" "The Torah gives a whole book to sacrifice. Since the temple fell, what takes its place, and who said so?"

label: Jewish · if they say
title: "Repentance, prayer and charity atone now."
text: Scripture commands all three, and never says they replace the blood. Daniel repented and prayed in exile, and still confessed that he had no righteousness of his own to plead, only God's great compassion (Dan 9:18). "Where does God say He changed the means of atonement?"

label: Jewish · if they say
title: "God doesn't want sacrifice. Hosea 6:6, Psalm 51:16."
text: Those verses rebuke sacrifice offered with a heart far from God. David's psalm ends with God delighting in righteous sacrifices on His altar (Ps 51:19). God was not cancelling Leviticus; He was demanding a broken heart with it.

label: Jewish · if they say
title: "The prayers of our lips replace the bulls. Hosea 14:2."
text: Hosea calls Israel to return with words of confession. He does not say words pay for sin. Someone still has to bear it. (Isa 53:6)

label: Jewish · if they say
title: "I'm a good person. I keep the commandments."
text: Ask which one they have kept perfectly, and walk through a few. Go to The Way of the Master. The Law was given to show sin, and Moses himself said the people would not keep it. (Deut 31:27–29; Deut 27:26)

label: Jewish · if they say
title: "I'm Jewish. I'm already in the covenant."
text: Isaiah, Jeremiah and John the Baptist all preached repentance to people in the covenant. God requires a circumcised heart. (Deut 10:16; Jer 4:4; Matt 3:9; Rom 2:28–29)

label: Jewish · play
title: Who is the Messiah? (when he comes, what he does, who he is)
text: "What do you think the Messiah will do when he comes, and how will you recognize him?" "If the Messiah had already come, how would you know?"

label: Jewish · if they say
title: "The Messiah brings world peace. There is no peace, so Jesus is not the Messiah."
text: He will bring it. The prophets give two pictures, a suffering Servant and a reigning King, and the rabbis saw the tension themselves and proposed two Messiahs, one of whom is killed [Talmud, Sukkah 52a]. Scripture's answer is one Messiah who comes twice. He dealt with sin first, because peace with God has to come before peace on earth. (Isa 53:5; Isa 2:4; Zech 14:4, 9)

label: Jewish · if they say
title: "God is not a man. Numbers 23:19."
text: That verse says God does not lie or change His mind the way a man does. It does not say God cannot take on flesh. He appeared to Abraham and ate with him (Gen 18:1–2), and Isaiah calls the child born "Mighty God" (Isa 9:6).

label: Jewish · if they say
title: "The Messiah is a man, not God."
text: He is both. Go to The Trinity and use Ps 110:1, Isa 9:6 and Dan 7:13–14 from this play.

label: Jewish · if they say
title: "Isaiah 7:14 says 'young woman,' not 'virgin.'"
text: The word is almah, a young unmarried woman, and Jewish translators before Jesus was born rendered it in Greek with the word for virgin [Septuagint]. A young woman giving birth is no sign at all. But don't make this your lead text; Isaiah 53 and Daniel 9 carry more weight in this conversation.

label: Jewish · objection
title: "The servant in Isaiah 53 is Israel."
text: This Servant restores Israel, is sinless, suffers willingly and dies for "my people." None of that fits the nation Isaiah calls sinful. The oldest Jewish readings took him to be Messiah [Targum Jonathan; Sanhedrin 98b]. Run Play 1. "If he dies for the people, how can he be the people?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "Jesus didn't bring peace, so he isn't the Messiah."
text: The prophets show Messiah suffering and Messiah reigning. One Messiah, two comings. He dealt with sin first; He will reign on David's throne and the nations will learn war no more. "Which does a sinner need first: peace on earth, or peace with God?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "'Hear, O Israel, the LORD is one.' The Trinity is idolatry."
text: We confess the Shema. One God, one Being. The Hebrew Scriptures themselves show more: "Let Us make man," Yahweh sending His Servant and His Spirit, and David's Lord seated beside Yahweh. See The Trinity. "Who is David's 'Lord' in Psalm 110?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "God is not a man."
text: Numbers 23:19 says God does not lie like a man. It does not say He cannot come in flesh. He appeared to Abraham as a man, and the child of Isaiah 9 is called Mighty God. "Is anything too hard for Yahweh?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "No one can die for another's sins. Ezekiel 18."
text: Ezekiel is answering people who blamed their fathers for their own judgment; each sinner answers for his own sin. That is the problem, not the solution. The whole sacrificial system is an innocent substitute bearing guilt, and Isaiah says Yahweh laid our iniquity on the Servant. "Then what was the goat on Yom Kippur doing?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "God hates human sacrifice."
text: He forbids men to offer their children to idols. Here it is God who gives, and the Servant who willingly gives himself. Yahweh was pleased to crush him, and he poured out himself to death. No one took his life from him. "Who is the offerer in Isaiah 53:10?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "We don't need a sacrifice. We repent."
text: Repentance is commanded, and it is not payment. A judge who lets the guilty go because they are sorry is not just, and God says He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. Someone bears it: you, or the substitute God provided. "If God just overlooks sin, is He still just?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "I'm a good person. God weighs the good against the bad."
text: Scripture has no scale like that. It says no one living is righteous before Him and that even our righteous deeds are stained. Use the commandments: see The Way of the Master. "Have you loved God with all your heart every day of your life?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "If I believe in Jesus I stop being Jewish."
text: Jesus is Jewish. So were the apostles and the whole first church, thousands in Jerusalem, many of them priests. Paul said, "I too am an Israelite." Following Israel's Messiah is the most Jewish thing a person can do. Do admit the cost: family may treat it as betrayal, and Jesus said He is worth it. "Was Paul still Jewish after the Damascus road?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "Christians have persecuted us for centuries."
text: Agree, and grieve it. Crusades, expulsions and pogroms were done in Christ's name against Christ's commands. They were sin. Judge Jesus by Jesus: He wept over Jerusalem and prayed for those who crucified Him. "Would you judge Moses by the Israelites who made the golden calf?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "The New Testament is antisemitic."
text: It was written by Jews about a Jewish Messiah, and its hard words to Israel are no harder than Isaiah's or Jeremiah's. It says salvation is from the Jews, that the gospel is for the Jew first, and that God has not rejected His people. "Was Isaiah antisemitic when he called Israel a sinful nation?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "Jesus broke the Torah and abolished it."
text: He said He came to fulfill the Law and the Prophets, not abolish them, and no one could convict Him of sin. What He rejected were traditions added to God's word. And God Himself promised a new covenant unlike Sinai. "Which commandment of Moses did Jesus break?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "If Jesus were the Messiah, the rabbis would have believed."
text: Isaiah foretold the opposite: "Who has believed our message?" The Servant is despised and rejected by his own. Yet thousands of Jews did believe, including many priests. Paul says a partial hardening has come on Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in, and then all Israel will be saved. "Did Israel's leaders usually listen to the prophets God sent?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "Christians say the church has replaced Israel. God is done with us."
text: Scripture does not say so. God tied His promise to Israel to the sun, moon and stars. Within the nation there has always been a believing remnant, and Paul says the day is coming when the nation and the remnant are the same: all Israel will be saved, when they look on the One they pierced [Abner Chou; MacArthur]. "Why are there still Jewish people on earth, when the Hittites and Amorites are gone?"

label: Jewish · objection
title: "I'm Jewish, but I'm not religious."
text: Most Jewish people you meet are here. Don't argue rabbinics. Ask what they think happens after death, use the commandments, and then show them Isaiah 53 as something from their own heritage they may never have seen. See The Gospel. "Have you ever read the prophets for yourself?"

label: Jewish · quick card
title: Isa 53:5–6: "Who is this, pierced for someone else's sins?"

label: Jewish · quick card
title: Isa 53:8–10: "He is cut off from the land of the living, and then prolongs his days. How?"

label: Jewish · quick card
title: Lev 17:11: "God says the blood makes atonement. With no temple, what is yours?"

label: Jewish · quick card
title: Dan 9:26: "The Anointed One is cut off before the temple falls. The temple fell in AD 70. Who was it?"

label: Jewish · quick card
title: Zech 12:10: "God says, 'They will look on Me whom they have pierced.' When was God pierced?"

label: Jewish · quick card
title: Jer 31:31–34: "God promised a new covenant, not like Sinai. Has it come?"

label: Hindu · play
title: Karma or the cross? (how the debt is paid)
text: "What do you believe happens to you when you die?" "Do you think you are closer to moksha than you were ten years ago? How can you tell?"

label: Hindu · if they say
title: "Grace is unjust. Everyone must pay for their own deeds."
text: God agrees that sin must be paid for; He does not wave it away. That is why the cross was necessary. Justice was done there, on a willing substitute. (Rom 3:25–26; Isa 53:5–6)

label: Hindu · if they say
title: "Suffering is the result of past lives."
text: Jesus was asked that very question about a man born blind: "Who sinned, this man or his parents?" He said neither. And think what the idea does: it tells the child in the slum that she deserved it. Jesus touched the people karma tells you to leave alone. See The problem of evil. (John 9:1–3; Luke 13:1–5; Matt 8:2–3)

label: Hindu · if they say
title: "I follow the path of devotion. My god gives grace too."
text: Ask how the god deals with the guilt. Does anyone pay, or is it just overlooked? Only at the cross is the debt actually settled, by a God who really entered history, died and rose. (Heb 9:22; 1 Cor 15:3–4)

label: Hindu · if they say
title: "I don't remember past lives, but I trust the teaching."
text: Why should a person suffer for deeds he cannot remember and so cannot repent of? Scripture has every person answer for the life he actually lived. (2 Cor 5:10; Ezek 18:20)

label: Hindu · play
title: The God who made you (Creator, not the creation)
text: "When you pray, who is listening? Is God a someone, or a something?" "If everything is God, is evil God too?"

label: Hindu · if they say
title: "The images are only aids. We worship the one reality behind them."
text: Israel said the same of the golden calf: "a feast to Yahweh." God still called it great sin. He decides how He is worshiped. (Ex 32:4–5; Deut 4:15–16; John 4:24)

label: Hindu · if they say
title: "Jesus is an avatar, like Krishna."
text: An avatar comes many times and only appears as a man. Jesus became truly man once, died a real death for sins, rose bodily, and said no one comes to the Father except through Him. He leaves no room on the shelf. (Heb 9:26; Luke 24:39; John 14:6)

label: Hindu · if they say
title: "I am one with God. The self is divine."
text: That is the oldest lie: "You will be like God." You get tired, you forget, you sin, you die. You are a creature, made in God's image, which is honor enough, and you need a Savior. (Gen 3:5; Isa 31:3; Ps 100:3)

label: Hindu · if they say
title: "My religion is far older than yours."
text: Age is not truth, and the God of the Bible is the Creator before any religion. He was at the beginning. (Gen 1:1; Ps 90:2)

label: Hindu · objection
title: "All religions are paths up the same mountain."
text: The religions disagree about what is at the top: a personal Creator, an impersonal oneness, or nothing. And who is standing high enough to see that all paths meet? Only God has that view, and He has spoken. "How do you know they all arrive?"

label: Hindu · objection
title: "I already believe in Jesus. He is one of my gods."
text: The Jesus of the Gospels refuses that place. He said to love Him more than father or mother, and that whoever is not with Him is against Him. To honor Him among others is not to believe Him. MacArthur's picture for this is Dagon: the Philistines set the ark of God beside their idol, and in the morning the idol was on its face, and the next morning broken. The living God will not share a shelf. "What did Jesus say about other ways to the Father?"

label: Hindu · objection
title: "Christianity is a Western religion."
text: Jesus was born in Asia, and by long tradition the gospel reached India in the first century. Scripture's vision is every tribe, tongue and nation before the throne. Christ is not the West's god; He is the Lord of all. "Was Jesus a Westerner?"

label: Hindu · objection
title: "Karma explains suffering better than your God does."
text: It explains it by blaming the sufferer, and it offers no one to help. The Bible says the world is fallen through sin, that God Himself entered the suffering, and that He will end it. "What does karma say to a suffering child?"

label: Hindu · objection
title: "We will be reborn. There is always another chance."
text: Scripture says we die once and then face judgment. And the teaching itself gives no hope: the debt grows each life. Jesus offers not another round but eternal life now. "If there were no next life, would you be ready?"

label: Hindu · objection
title: "God is in everything and everyone."
text: God is present everywhere, but He is not everything. He made the world and is distinct from it. If all is God, there is no difference between good and evil, and no one to pray to. "Is cruelty also God?"

label: Hindu · objection
title: "Meditation and yoga give me real peace and real experiences."
text: An experience can be real and not be true. Scripture warns that Satan disguises himself as an angel of light and tells us to test the spirits. Peace with God is not a feeling produced by technique; it is a standing, given through Christ. "Does the peace deal with your guilt, or only quiet it?"

label: Hindu · objection
title: "Christians are intolerant to say only Jesus saves."
text: We did not make the claim; Jesus did. If a doctor has the one cure, telling you so is love. And we say it as people who needed the cure ourselves. "If it were true, would you want me to tell you?"

label: Hindu · objection
title: "My family would be dishonored if I became a Christian."
text: Do not make light of it. Jesus said it would cost exactly this, and promised a hundredfold family in His people and eternal life. Then be that family. "What would make Him worth that cost?"

label: Hindu · quick card
title: Heb 9:27: "One death, then judgment. If that is true, what happens to the plan of many lives?"

label: Hindu · quick card
title: Isa 45:5–6: "God says there is no other. Can He be one of many?"

label: Hindu · quick card
title: Ps 115:4–8: "Can something a man made hear a man's prayer?"

label: Hindu · quick card
title: John 14:6: "Did Jesus say He was a way, or the way?"

label: Hindu · quick card
title: Col 2:13–14: "What did God do with the record of debt?"

label: Hindu · quick card
title: Matt 11:28: "Who else offers rest instead of more work?"

label: Buddhist · play
title: Who forgives you? (the problem is sin, not desire)
text: "What do you think is the deepest problem with people?" "Have you ever done something you knew was wrong? What did you do with the guilt?"

label: Buddhist · if they say
title: "There is no sin, only ignorance and unskillful action."
text: Then no one has ever truly been wronged, and no cruelty is truly evil. You don't live as if that were so. Jeff Durbin's observation to a skeptic applies: when you speak of compassion and human worth, you are borrowing from a world God made. (Rom 1:19–20; Rom 2:15)

label: Buddhist · if they say
title: "There is no self, so there is no one to be guilty."
text: Then there is no one to be compassionate to, and no one to reach nirvana. You love real people. Scripture explains why: each is made in God's image. (Gen 1:27; Ps 139:13–14)

label: Buddhist · if they say
title: "I make merit to balance it."
text: How much is enough, and who keeps the account? Our best deeds are stained. A gift cannot be earned. (Isa 64:6; Titus 3:5; Eph 2:8–9)

label: Buddhist · if they say
title: "Amida Buddha saves by grace." (Pure Land)
text: You are right to see that we cannot save ourselves. But grace needs a real Savior who actually dealt with sin in history. Jesus lived, died under Pontius Pilate and rose; witnesses saw Him. (1 Cor 15:3–8; Acts 4:12)

label: Buddhist · play
title: The end of suffering (extinguished, or made new)
text: "What is nirvana like? Is there a 'you' there to enjoy it?" "Is the goal to stop wanting, or to finally have what you were made for?"

label: Buddhist · if they say
title: "Attachment is the cause of suffering, so the wise love without attachment."
text: God so loved the world that He gave His Son. Love that costs nothing is not love. The Bible's answer to loss is not caring less, but a resurrection in which nothing given to God is lost. (John 3:16; John 15:13; 1 Thess 4:13–14)

label: Buddhist · if they say
title: "Everything is impermanent."
text: Everything created, yes. "The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever." There is One who does not change. (Isa 40:8; Mal 3:6; Heb 13:8)

label: Buddhist · if they say
title: "Meditation has ended a lot of my suffering."
text: It may have quieted your mind. It has not dealt with death, guilt or God. Jesus offers rest for the soul and a peace the world cannot give. (Matt 11:28–29; John 14:27)

label: Buddhist · if they say
title: "The Buddha was enlightened. Why not follow both?"
text: They point opposite ways: no God or the living God; no self or an eternal soul; escape or resurrection. And only one of them rose from the dead. See The resurrection.

label: Buddhist · objection
title: "Buddhism is a philosophy, not a religion. It fits with any belief."
text: The Buddha's teaching has no Creator and no soul. Jesus teaches both, and says He is the only way. They cannot both be right. "Which of the two would you give up?"

label: Buddhist · objection
title: "There is no creator. The universe has always cycled."
text: Something that changes and decays cannot be eternal and self-explaining. Creation shows God's eternal power so plainly that men are without excuse. See Worldviews: how do you know?. "Why is there something and not nothing?"

label: Buddhist · objection
title: "Desire is the root of suffering."
text: Wrong desire is. God made us to desire, and commands us to delight in Him. Sin is what brought suffering in. "Is the desire to end suffering also a problem?"

label: Buddhist · objection
title: "There is no self."
text: Then who is practicing, and who is reborn? You know you are someone. God made you in His image and knows you by name. "Who is the one asking?"

label: Buddhist · objection
title: "I'm responsible for my own liberation."
text: That is honest, and it is the bad news. No one keeps the path perfectly. The gospel is for the helpless. "How is the path going?"

label: Buddhist · objection
title: "Karma is perfectly fair."
text: Fair is exactly what we should fear. And with no judge, who administers it? Scripture has a Judge who is just, and who also made a way for mercy. "Do you want what you deserve?"

label: Buddhist · objection
title: "Christians believe in hell. Buddhism is more compassionate."
text: Traditional Buddhism has hells too, for ages. The question is what is true. The same Jesus who warned of hell died to keep people out of it. See Hell and eternal judgment. "If the warning is true, is it unkind to give it?"

label: Buddhist · objection
title: "All teachers say the same thing: be kind."
text: They share some ethics and differ on everything underneath. Only Jesus claimed to be God, died for sins and rose. Kindness does not remove guilt. "Did the Buddha claim to forgive sins?"

label: Buddhist · objection
title: "I just live in the present moment."
text: Good, as far as it goes. But the present moment is moving toward a day God has fixed. Wisdom numbers its days. "What happens in the moment after your last one?"

label: Buddhist · quick card
title: Gen 1:1: "If there is a Creator, do we answer to Him?"

label: Buddhist · quick card
title: Ps 51:4: "When you do wrong, who is wronged, and who can forgive it?"

label: Buddhist · quick card
title: Ps 16:11: "What if the answer to desire is not less of it, but the right object?"

label: Buddhist · quick card
title: John 11:25–26: "The Buddha is in his grave. What did Jesus say at one?"

label: Buddhist · quick card
title: John 19:30: "'Strive on,' or 'It is finished'?"

label: Buddhist · quick card
title: Rev 21:4: "Who can promise an end to suffering and has the power to do it?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · play
title: Are you God? (Creator and creature)
text: "When you say 'the Universe,' do you mean a someone or a something? Does it know your name?" "If we are all divine, why is the world like this?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · if they say
title: "Jesus said, 'The kingdom of God is within you.'"
text: He said it to Pharisees who were plotting against Him; He was not telling them they were divine. The King was standing in their midst. The same Jesus said that what comes from within a man defiles him. (Luke 17:20–21; Mark 7:20–23)

label: New Age / Spiritualist · if they say
title: "Jesus reached Christ consciousness, and so can we."
text: "Christ" is not a state of mind; it is a title, the Messiah, and it belongs to one Man. He warned that many would come saying "I am the Christ." (Matt 16:16; Matt 24:4–5, 23–24; 1 John 2:22)

label: New Age / Spiritualist · if they say
title: "We're all children of God."
text: All are made by God. But the right to become children of God is given to those who receive Christ and believe in His name. (John 1:12; Gal 3:26; Acts 17:28–29)

label: New Age / Spiritualist · if they say
title: "That's your truth."
text: Is that statement true for both of us, or only for you? And follow it through: if truth and right are personal, the rapist has his truth too, and no one can say he was wrong. You don't believe that. Some things are wrong for everyone, which means there is a standard above all of us. Jesus did not say He had a truth. He said, "I am the truth." See Faith and reason. (John 14:6; John 18:37)

label: New Age / Spiritualist · play
title: Which spirit? (guides, readings and the test)
text: "How do you know that your guides, or the cards, are telling you the truth?" "Has anything you've encountered ever frightened you?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · if they say
title: "My guides are loving. They only tell me good things."
text: A spirit that never names your sin and never points you to Christ's cross is telling you what the serpent told Eve: you will not die. Love tells the truth. (Gen 3:4; Jer 6:14; Gal 1:8)

label: New Age / Spiritualist · if they say
title: "I talk to my grandmother. It comforts me."
text: I'm sorry for your loss. Scripture says the dead do not return to guide us, and forbids seeking them, so whatever is answering is not her. The God of all comfort invites you to bring that grief to Him. (Luke 16:26; Deut 18:11; 2 Cor 1:3–4)

label: New Age / Spiritualist · if they say
title: "It's just for fun. Astrology is harmless."
text: God does not call it harmless, and it trains you to look to creation for what only the Creator gives. He made the stars; ask Him. (Deut 4:19; Isa 47:13; James 1:5)

label: New Age / Spiritualist · if they say
title: "Christians are afraid of everything."
text: Not afraid: free. "Greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world." We simply don't go where our Father said not to. (1 John 4:4; 2 Tim 1:7)

label: New Age / Spiritualist · objection
title: "I'm spiritual, not religious."
text: Jesus was hard on empty religion too. But "spiritual" still has to answer: which spirit, and is it true? The alternative to dead religion is not making it up; it is knowing the living God. "What does 'spiritual' mean to you?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · objection
title: "The Universe has my back."
text: An impersonal universe cannot love, hear or keep a promise. What you are hoping for is a Father. There is one, and He has a name. "Has the Universe ever forgiven you?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · objection
title: "I manifest my reality. Thoughts become things."
text: Then every suffering person caused their own cancer, and you carry a weight no one can bear. Scripture says God rules and we ask: "If the Lord wills." That is freedom, not control. "Did the child in the hospital manifest that?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · objection
title: "We are all one. Separation is an illusion."
text: If all is one, there is no real difference between love and cruelty. The Bible says the separation that matters is real: our sins have separated us from God. And it can be healed. "Is evil part of the oneness?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · objection
title: "Right and wrong are personal. Everyone has their own truth."
text: Then no one is ever wrong. The rapist was living his truth. And if you say society decides instead, then what Hitler's Germany did to the Jews was good for them at the time. You know both are false, so there is a standard above every person and every nation. See Morality and justice. "Was that wrong for everyone, or just not your preference?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · objection
title: "There's no sin, only lower vibrations and lessons."
text: You don't believe that when you are betrayed. Wrong is real, guilt is real, and renaming it does not remove it. Blood does. "Have you ever needed to be forgiven?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · objection
title: "I've lived many lives."
text: Scripture says once, then judgment. And notice that past-life "memories" are always of someone interesting. More to the point: if many lives haven't fixed us, another won't. "If this is the only one, are you ready?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · objection
title: "Jesus was a great spiritual teacher, like the others."
text: Great teachers don't claim to be God, forgive sins and say all will be judged by them, unless it is true. He is not on the list; He is in a category of one. "Have you read what He actually claimed?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · objection
title: "The church suppressed the real, mystical Jesus."
text: The "hidden" gospels are second-century and later, and read nothing like eyewitness accounts. The four Gospels come from the first century and the apostles' circle. See Is the Bible reliable?. "Which source is closest to the events?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · objection
title: "Crystals, sage and energy work heal me."
text: God made stones and plants good, and they are not gods. To look to created things for protection and power is the exchange Romans 1 describes. Bring the need to the One who made them. "What is it you are hoping to be healed of?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · objection
title: "Everything happens for a reason, and it all works out for everyone."
text: God does rule all things, and He promises good to those who love Him and are called by Him. For those who refuse Him, Scripture promises judgment. Don't take the comfort without the Christ. "Whose reason? Who is behind it?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · quick card
title: Gen 3:4–5: "Who first said, 'You will be like God'?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · quick card
title: Jer 17:9: "If the heart is deceitful, is 'follow your heart' safe advice?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · quick card
title: Deut 18:10–12: "What does God say about mediums, fortune-telling and divination?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · quick card
title: 2 Cor 11:14: "If a spirit of darkness came to you, how would it look?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · quick card
title: John 14:6: "Did Jesus say 'find your truth,' or 'I am the truth'?"

label: New Age / Spiritualist · quick card
title: Heb 9:27: "How many times does a person die?"

label: Satanist · play
title: Your own god? (the atheist kinds: Church of Satan, Satanic Temple)
text: "What does Satan stand for, to you?" "If you are your own highest authority, who do you answer to when you are wrong?"

label: Satanist · if they say
title: "Christianity is for the weak. It's a slave religion."
text: It is for the guilty, which is everyone. As for weak: its founder went to a Roman cross on purpose, forgave the men nailing Him there and walked out of His grave. Self-indulgence takes no strength at all; any child can do it. (John 10:17–18; Luke 23:34; Titus 2:11–12)

label: Satanist · if they say
title: "Our tenets are more moral than your Bible: compassion, reason, justice."
text: Those are good things, and they are borrowed. In a world with no God, why is compassion binding on anyone, and why is justice more than opinion? If each person decides, the rapist is never wrong. See Morality and justice. (Rom 2:14–15; Mic 6:8)

label: Satanist · if they say
title: "I don't hurt anyone. I just live for myself."
text: The first and greatest commandment is to love God with all your heart, and living for yourself breaks it every hour. And you have hurt people; all of us have. (Matt 22:37–38; Rom 3:23)

label: Satanist · if they say
title: "My body is mine alone."
text: You did not make it and you cannot keep it. It is on loan from the One who knit it together, and He will ask for an account. (Ps 139:13–14; 1 Cor 6:19–20; Heb 9:27)

label: Satanist · play
title: The real Satan (for those who honor him, and for the occult)
text: "What do you believe Satan is, and what has he done for you?" "Do you know how the Bible says his story ends?"

label: Satanist · if they say
title: "He gives me power. It works."
text: He offered Jesus all the kingdoms of the world for one act of worship. He pays in things that cannot be kept, and the price is you. A girl in Philippi had real power from a spirit, and she was a slave. (Matt 4:8–10; Mark 8:36; Acts 16:16–18)

label: Satanist · if they say
title: "Lucifer is the light-bringer who freed us with knowledge. God is the tyrant."
text: He promised they would be like God and would not die. They got shame, fear and a grave. Then look at who the "tyrant" turned out to be: the One who laid down His life for His enemies. The thief comes to steal, kill and destroy; the Good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep. (Gen 3:4–10; John 10:10–11; Rom 5:8)

label: Satanist · if they say
title: "I've gone too far. I gave myself to him."
text: Your soul was never yours to sign away: "All souls are Mine," God says. Jesus freed a man who had a legion of demons, and saved the man who called himself the foremost of sinners. No pact outranks His blood. (Ezek 18:4; Mark 5:15; 1 Tim 1:15; Col 2:14–15)

label: Satanist · if they say
title: "I'm afraid of what happens if I leave."
text: No one can snatch Christ's sheep out of His hand. Submit to God, resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Get rid of the objects and books, as the Ephesians did, and get into a faithful church. (John 10:28–29; James 4:7; Acts 19:18–20)

label: Satanist · objection
title: "We don't worship the devil. Satanism is atheism."
text: Understood, and most do mean that. Then the questions are the atheist's: where do reason, worth and right and wrong come from? See the Atheist plays. And notice what you took for a mascot. "Of all symbols, why that one?"

label: Satanist · objection
title: "Christians invented lies about us. The Satanic Panic."
text: False accusation is sin, and where Christians spread stories that were not true, they broke the ninth commandment. That does not make the philosophy true. Judge it by what it teaches. "Setting the rumors aside, is 'be your own god' true?"

label: Satanist · objection
title: "In the Bible, God kills millions and Satan kills a handful."
text: The Giver of life has the right to take it, and every death He decrees is just. The devil is called a murderer from the beginning because he brought death on the whole race with a lie. And only One of them died to give life back. "Who brought death into the world in Genesis 3?"

label: Satanist · objection
title: "Religion is slavery. I bow to no one."
text: Everyone serves something: appetite, approval, anger, self. The question is which master is good. Christ's yoke is easy, and He calls His servants friends. "What can you not say no to?"

label: Satanist · objection
title: "We fight for freedom and against theocracy."
text: Faith cannot be forced, and Christians should say so first. But freedom from God is not freedom; it is the far country, and it ends at the pig trough. The Father is still watching the road. "Free for what?"

label: Satanist · objection
title: "I renounced my baptism."
text: Water never saved anyone, so there was nothing magic to undo. What matters is not a ceremony but Christ, and He receives those who come to Him, including those who once cursed Him. "What would it take for you to come back?"

label: Satanist · objection
title: "Blasphemy is funny. Hail Satan."
text: God is not shaken; He who sits in the heavens laughs. But ask why it is always Jesus' name and never Zeus's. People do not rage at what they think is nothing. His patience with you is kindness, meant to lead you to repentance. "Why does He bother you so much?"

label: Satanist · objection
title: "Hell is a threat to control people."
text: Jesus, who warned of it most, is the one who died to keep people out of it. A warning from someone who paid your way out is not a threat. See Hell and eternal judgment. "If it is real, would you want to be told?"

label: Satanist · objection
title: "I've seen things. Spirits are real, and they answer me."
text: I believe you. Scripture says they are real, that they lie, and that God forbids contact with them because they destroy. Test them by what they say about Jesus. "What do they say about the cross?"

label: Satanist · quick card
title: Gen 3:4–5: "Who first said, 'You will be like God'? How did it turn out?"

label: Satanist · quick card
title: John 8:34: "Is doing what you want freedom, or slavery?"

label: Satanist · quick card
title: John 8:44: "What does Jesus say the devil is, from the beginning?"

label: Satanist · quick card
title: Col 2:15: "What happened to the powers of darkness at the cross?"

label: Satanist · quick card
title: Rev 20:10: "How does the devil's story end?"

label: Satanist · quick card
title: Col 1:13–14: "What does God do for those in the domain of darkness?"

label: Oneness Pentecostal · play
title: Who was Jesus talking to? (Father and Son are distinct persons)
text: "When Jesus prayed in the garden, who was He praying to?" "At Jesus' baptism, whose voice came from heaven?"

label: Oneness Pentecostal · if they say
title: "That was His human nature praying to His divine nature."
text: Natures don't pray; persons do. And John 17:5 speaks of glory shared before the world was, before there was any humanity to pray. "Who is 'Me' and who is 'You' before Bethlehem?"

label: Oneness Pentecostal · if they say
title: "'I and the Father are one' (John 10:30)."
text: Amen, one in being. But the verb is plural: "I and the Father, we are one." He did not say "I am the Father." And the verse before distinguishes "My hand" and "My Father's hand."

label: Oneness Pentecostal · if they say
title: "'He who has seen Me has seen the Father' (John 14:9)."
text: The next verse reads, "I am in the Father, and the Father is in Me… the Father abiding in Me does His works." He reveals the Father perfectly because He is God the Son. He does not say He is the Father. (John 1:18)

label: Oneness Pentecostal · if they say
title: "Isaiah 9:6 calls Him 'Everlasting Father.'"
text: It is a title of the Messiah-King: literally "Father of eternity," the one who is eternal and cares for His people as a father. The same book has Yahweh sending His Servant and His Spirit (Isa 48:16). Nowhere does the New Testament call Jesus "the Father."

label: Oneness Pentecostal · play
title: The Son before Bethlehem (the eternal Son)
text: "Did the Son of God exist before Mary conceived?" "Who made all things: the Father alone, or the Father through the Son?"

label: Oneness Pentecostal · if they say
title: "'The Son' is the humanity that began at Bethlehem (Luke 1:35)."
text: Luke 1:35 says why the child would be called Son of God. It does not say the Son began then. The Son made the world (Col 1:16; Heb 1:2). A human nature that did not yet exist made nothing.

label: Oneness Pentecostal · if they say
title: "The Word was God's thought or plan, not a person."
text: A plan is not "with God" face to face, does not make all things, and is not called "He" and "the only begotten from the Father." (John 1:2–3, 14, 18)

label: Oneness Pentecostal · if they say
title: "God is a Spirit, and Jesus is that Spirit in flesh."
text: God is spirit, yes. And the Spirit is sent by the Father and the Son and is called "another" Helper (John 14:16; John 15:26). Jesus is the Son incarnate, not the Father or the Spirit incarnate.

label: Oneness Pentecostal · play
title: What saves? (Acts 2:38, the formula and tongues)
text: "If a man repents and trusts Christ on his deathbed and never gets to the water, is he saved?" "Is a person saved by what Christ did, or by Christ plus being baptized with the right words?"

label: Oneness Pentecostal · if they say
title: "Acts 2:38: be baptized 'for the forgiveness of your sins.'"
text: Peter's very next sermons promise forgiveness to those who repent and believe, with no mention of baptism (Acts 3:19; Acts 10:43). Baptism is the public confession of the repentance that receives forgiveness. Cornelius had the Spirit before the water.

label: Oneness Pentecostal · if they say
title: "The apostles always baptized in Jesus' name, never 'Father, Son and Spirit.'"
text: "In the name of" means by the authority of and with reference to Jesus, as against John's baptism or a Jewish washing. Luke words it four different ways (Acts 2:38; Acts 8:16; Acts 10:48; Acts 19:5), which is not how anyone records a fixed formula.

label: Oneness Pentecostal · if they say
title: "Matthew 28:19 says 'name,' singular, and that name is Jesus."
text: One name because one God. Then three are listed, each with "the": the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit. That is the Trinity in one sentence.

label: Oneness Pentecostal · if they say
title: "You haven't received the Holy Ghost unless you've spoken in tongues."
text: Anyone who does not have the Spirit does not belong to Christ at all, and every believer is sealed with the Spirit when he believes. (Rom 8:9; Eph 1:13–14) Our church also holds that the sign gifts ceased with the apostles.

label: Oneness Pentecostal · if they say
title: "John 3:5: born of water and the Spirit."
text: Jesus expected Nicodemus, a teacher of Israel, to know this from the Old Testament: clean water and a new Spirit in Ezekiel 36:25–27. It is the new birth God gives, and the same chapter says whoever believes has eternal life. (John 3:10, 16)

label: Oneness Pentecostal · objection
title: "The Trinity is three gods."
text: It is not, and say so first. One God, one Being. Within that one Being are three persons who are each fully God. Three gods would be three beings. Most people who reject the Trinity are rejecting something Christians do not believe. "If I told you I believe in one God, not three, what would you say the Trinity is?"

label: Oneness Pentecostal · objection
title: "The word 'Trinity' isn't in the Bible."
text: Neither is "Oneness," "incarnation" or "Bible." The question is whether the teaching is there: one God; the Father, the Son and the Spirit are each God; and they are distinct from one another. Believe all three and you have the Trinity. "Which of those three statements does Scripture not teach?"

label: Oneness Pentecostal · objection
title: "The Trinity was invented at Nicaea in 325."
text: Nicaea was about whether the Son is fully God, against Arius. Long before it, Christians baptized in the threefold name and were already rejecting the teaching that the Father and the Son are one person (it was called Sabellianism in the third century). "If it began in 325, why does Matthew 28:19 read the way it does?"

label: Oneness Pentecostal · objection
title: "'In Him all the fullness of Deity dwells in bodily form.' Jesus is all of God."
text: Amen: Jesus is fully God, nothing lacking. That is the deity of the Son. It does not say the Son is the Father. The same letter thanks "the Father" who transferred us to the kingdom of "His beloved Son." "Who is the Father of the beloved Son in chapter 1?"

label: Oneness Pentecostal · objection
title: "God was manifest in the flesh (1 Tim 3:16)."
text: We agree that God the Son became flesh. "The Word became flesh," and the Word was with God. It was the Son who was sent, not the Father. "According to 1 John 4:14, who sent whom?"

label: Oneness Pentecostal · objection
title: "Jesus said, 'I have come in My Father's name.' Jesus is the Father's name."
text: To come in someone's name is to come with his authority. In the same breath Jesus says another may come "in his own name." He comes from the Father and is not the Father. "Can you be sent by yourself?"

label: Oneness Pentecostal · objection
title: "Zechariah 14:9: Yahweh will be one, and His name one."
