title: Acts 14:17: "What witness has God left of Himself every day?"

label: Deist · quick card
title: Acts 26:8: "If God made the world, why is raising the dead incredible?"

label: Deist · quick card
title: Luke 18:19: "Who does Jesus say is good?"

label: Deist · quick card
title: Rom 5:8: "What did God do that nature could never tell you?"

label: Secular Humanist · play
title: Where does human worth come from? (the image of God)
text: "What makes a human life valuable?" "Why is it wrong to treat people as things?"

label: Secular Humanist · if they say
title: "We give each other worth by agreement."
text: Then a society can agree to take it away, and has. Hitler's Germany agreed that Jews had none. If agreement is the standard, that was good for them at the time, and no outsider could call it evil. A right that the majority grants, the majority can revoke. Only a worth given by God stands over every government. (Acts 5:29; Prov 22:2)

label: Secular Humanist · if they say
title: "Morality evolved because cooperation helps us survive."
text: That would explain why we feel obligations, not why we have any. And evolution "favors" cruelty as readily as kindness when it works. See Morality and justice.

label: Secular Humanist · if they say
title: "Religion has done more harm than good."
text: Much evil has been done in God's name, against Christ's commands. But the worst slaughters of the last century were carried out by regimes that had officially abolished God. And look at who built the hospitals and ended the slave trade. Judge Christ by Christ. (Matt 7:16–20; James 1:27; John 13:35)

label: Secular Humanist · if they say
title: "Science tells us what is true."
text: Science tells us what is, never what ought to be, and "only science gives knowledge" is not itself a finding of science. See Faith and reason.

label: Secular Humanist · play
title: Can we save ourselves? (the heart, and death)
text: "Do you think people are basically good?" "What would it take to fix the world?"

label: Secular Humanist · if they say
title: "Evil comes from poverty, ignorance and bad systems."
text: Those make things worse, and Christians should fight them. But the comfortable and educated sin as freely as anyone, only with better lawyers. Systems are made of hearts. (James 4:1–2; Mark 7:21)

label: Secular Humanist · if they say
title: "We make our own meaning."
text: A meaning you invent is a story you tell yourself, and it ends when you do. Solomon tried pleasure, work, wisdom and wealth and called it vapor. Meaning has to be given by the One who made you. (Eccl 1:2–3; Eccl 12:13–14; John 17:3)

label: Secular Humanist · if they say
title: "This life is all there is, so make the most of it."
text: Paul agrees that would follow: "If the dead are not raised, let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die." But Christ has been raised. See The resurrection. (1 Cor 15:32; 1 Cor 15:20)

label: Secular Humanist · if they say
title: "I don't need saving."
text: From what you have done, and from what is coming. Walk through a few commandments: see The Way of the Master. (Rom 3:19; Heb 9:27)

label: Secular Humanist · objection
title: "I believe in science, not faith."
text: Science is a gift, and it was born among people who believed a rational God made an orderly world. It cannot tell you why you matter, what is right or what happens when you die. "Which experiment shows that people have rights?"

label: Secular Humanist · objection
title: "Faith is believing without evidence."
text: Not in the Bible. Jesus presented Himself alive by many convincing proofs, and the apostles appealed to public facts. Faith is trust in One who has shown Himself trustworthy. "Where did you get that definition?"

label: Secular Humanist · objection
title: "Society decides what is right."
text: Then what Hitler's Germany did to the Jews was right, there and then, and the people who hid Jews were the wrongdoers. And if you retreat to "each person decides," the rapist is never wrong. Neither holds, so the standard is above both. See Morality and justice. "Was the Holocaust wrong even though their society approved it?"

label: Secular Humanist · objection
title: "Morality is about human wellbeing."
text: Whose wellbeing, measured how, and why should the strong care about the weak? "Wellbeing" quietly assumes that people have worth, which is the very thing to be explained. "Why ought I to care about a stranger's wellbeing?"

label: Secular Humanist · objection
title: "People are basically good."
text: History, the news and our own hearts say otherwise, and so does Jesus. The honest diagnosis is the first step to the cure. "Do you need a lock on your door?"

label: Secular Humanist · objection
title: "Religion is the cause of most wars and oppression."
text: Sinners are. They use religion, nation, race and economics alike. The officially godless states of the last century killed their own people by the tens of millions. "What did the regimes that abolished God put in His place?"

label: Secular Humanist · objection
title: "Keep your religion out of public life."
text: Everyone brings a view of what is good into public life. Humanism is one such view, with manifestos. The question is not whether a creed will shape the law, but which one. "Is your view of right and wrong allowed in?"

label: Secular Humanist · objection
title: "When you're dead, you're dead."
text: That is a belief, not a discovery. Scripture says judgment follows death, and God has given evidence by raising Jesus. "How do you know?"

label: Secular Humanist · objection
title: "I find meaning in family, work and making things better."
text: Those are good gifts. But gifts point to a Giver, and none of them survives the grave. You were made for more than what you can lose. "What happens to that meaning when those are taken?"

label: Secular Humanist · objection
title: "Christianity is anti-human: guilt, rules and fear."
text: It says you are made in God's image, loved at the cost of God's own Son, and offered life that death cannot end. Nothing has ever thought more of human beings. Guilt is real, and it is taken away. "What would you do with guilt if there were no forgiveness?"

label: Secular Humanist · quick card
title: Gen 1:27: "What gives a human being worth that an animal does not have?"

label: Secular Humanist · quick card
title: Jer 17:9: "Is the human heart the solution or the problem?"

label: Secular Humanist · quick card
title: Ps 146:3–4: "What happens to every human plan?"

label: Secular Humanist · quick card
title: Rom 7:18–19: "Do you always do the good you know?"

label: Secular Humanist · quick card
title: Mark 8:36: "What is the profit if you gain the world and lose your soul?"

label: Secular Humanist · quick card
title: Titus 3:4–5: "Who does the saving here?"

label: Atheist · play
title: Pin down the position
text: "Are you claiming God doesn't exist, or that you don't know?"

label: Atheist · if they say
title: "I just believe in one less god than you."
text: "You already reject gods who aren't there. I'm asking about the One you already know is there." (Rom 1:19–21)

label: Atheist · play
title: Design + life from life
text: "Have you ever seen something this ordered come from something non-intelligent?"

label: Atheist · play
title: The "borrowed capital" questions (presuppositional)
text: "Can I ask you about three things we both rely on every day: logic, right and wrong, and your own reasoning?" "Where do you get this idea of bad from?" (When they call something evil or unfair.) "What would count as evidence for you?" (When they say there's no evidence for God.) "Is morality objective, or is it opinion?" (When they say you're wrong about a moral issue.)

label: Atheist · play
title: The Resurrection (the center)
text: "If Jesus really rose from the dead, would you become a Christian?" "What about the people who didn't believe in Jesus, persecuted His followers, then said, 'I saw Jesus'?" (When they say it's a game of telephone.)

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Jesus is a copy of Horus / Osiris / Mithras."
text: Comes from pop media (Zeitgeist, Religulous), not the Egyptian sources. No virgin birth, no crucifixion, no resurrection in the primary texts. "Which primary Egyptian text says Horus was born of a virgin? Name it."

label: Atheist · objection
title: "It's like the Salem witch trials / a game of telephone."
text: Public execution under Pilate, guarded tomb, and eyewitnesses who were still alive when it was written (1 Cor 15:6, "most are still alive"). "Who dies for what they know is a lie?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Why do babies get cancer because Adam ate fruit?"
text: Federal headship. A head affects those he represents, like a mother's toxins affecting her unborn child. Adam's fall broke creation. Christ, the second Adam, restores it. "If God exists, wouldn't you expect Him to fix the fall? He did, in Christ."

label: Atheist · objection
title: "If God knew I'd reject Him, why create me? That's unjust."
text: God is just and owes no one mercy. No one is forced to reject Him: people reject Him because they love their sin, and they are responsible for it. Hell is the just penalty for real guilt, not a mistake. Yet God freely offers Christ to all who come, and no one who comes is turned away. "Is there anything you've done that a perfectly just judge should ignore?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "A jealous God who demands worship is vain."
text: Not all jealousy is sinful. A husband who's jealous over an unfaithful wife is rightly jealous. God made every breath you take, so He has a rightful claim. "If your wife slept with another man, would your jealousy be ugly, or just?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Heaven/hell is a game show: pick a door."
text: It's not a game show. It's a command and an invitation. God commands everyone to repent and offers Himself, the greatest good. Whoever refuses Him is responsible for that refusal. Full answer: Hell and eternal judgment. "It's not God playing games. You're playing games with Him."

label: Atheist · objection
title: "So many religions. How would I know which one?"
text: God has spoken, and He proved it publicly by raising Jesus from the dead. Only Christianity rests on a public resurrection, an event that is historically testable. Full answer: The exclusivity of Christ. "Which other religion stakes everything on a public event you can investigate?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Who created God?"
text: The question assumes everything needs a cause. It doesn't. Only what begins to exist needs a cause. God never began; He is uncaused by definition, the cause of everything outside Himself. Asking who made Him is a category mistake, like asking who made the One who was never made. "Does everything need a cause, or only things that begin to exist?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "I'm not 100% sure. I have doubts."
text: Faith isn't intellectual perfection. Jesus welcomes doubters who come to Him. "Do you believe Christ died for your sins and rose again? Will you turn from your sin and trust Him as Lord?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "There's no evidence for God."
text: Creation itself is the evidence: a universe that began, runs on laws, and holds minds and morals. And God gave proof to all by raising Jesus from the dead. "What would count as evidence for you?" Then: "Is the problem the evidence, or that you don't want God to be there?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Science has disproved God."
text: Science studies how creation works. It depends on order and laws it cannot explain, and it cannot tell you why anything exists or what is right. "Which experiment showed there is no God?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "If God is good, why is there so much evil and suffering?"
text: Calling something evil assumes a real standard of good. Scripture names the cause (the fall), shows God turning evil to good, entering suffering at the cross, and promising to end it. Full answer: The problem of evil. "By what standard do you call it evil?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "The Bible was written by men and is full of errors."
text: Men wrote as they were moved by the Holy Spirit. Ask for a specific error and read it together. "Which error? Let's look at it."

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Morality is decided by each person, or by society."
text: If each person decides, the rapist is never wrong; he was acting on his own truth. If society decides, what Hitler's Germany did to the Jews was good for them at the time. No one can live with either. Real right and wrong need a standard above every person and nation. See Morality and justice. "Was the Holocaust wrong even though their society approved?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "The God of the Old Testament is a moral monster."
text: To judge Him you need an objective standard, which only He supplies. He judged wicked nations after centuries of patience, He takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked, and He bore judgment Himself at the cross. "If there is no God, what makes anything objectively wrong?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Religion causes wars, and Christians are hypocrites."
text: People sin, which is exactly what the Bible says. Jesus condemned hypocrisy harder than anyone. Judge Christianity by Christ. "Does a counterfeit bill prove there's no real money?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "I'm a good person. I don't need God."
text: Good by whose standard? By God's law, none is righteous, and breaking one point makes us guilty of all. Then give the gospel: Christ died for sinners. "Have you ever lied, stolen, or hated someone? What does that make you before a perfect Judge?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Evolution explains life. We don't need a Creator."
text: Change in living things doesn't explain the first life, the information inside it, or the universe it lives in. And Scripture says God made everything in six days and made man directly, in His image. We are not the product of evolution. For the full case see The fallacy of evolution. "Where did the first life, and the information in it, come from?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Miracles are impossible."
text: Only if there is no God, which assumes the answer. If God made the universe, raising a man is not hard for Him. "If God created everything, is a resurrection too hard for Him?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "What about people who have never heard?"
text: Everyone has creation and conscience, and everyone suppresses them. No one is condemned for not hearing, but for sin. The Judge of all the earth will do right. And you have heard. "You've heard. What will you do with Jesus?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Faith is believing without evidence."
text: Biblical faith is trust in a Person on good grounds: eyewitness testimony and many convincing proofs. "Do you trust anyone on the basis of testimony?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Jesus never existed."
text: Paul received the resurrection report within a few years and met Peter and James, the Lord's brother, in person. "Who did Paul meet in Galatians 1:18–19?"

label: Atheist · quick card
title: "Are you claiming God doesn't exist, or that you don't know?" (Sets the burden.)

label: Atheist · quick card
title: "Have you ever seen something this ordered come from something non-intelligent?"

label: Atheist · quick card
title: "Life only comes from life. Where did the first life come from?"

label: Atheist · quick card
title: "No one dies for what they know is a lie." (1 Cor 15:3–8)

label: Atheist · quick card
title: "If heaven and hell were real, wouldn't you want to know before you die?"

label: Atheist · quick card
title: Rom 1:18–21: they know God and suppress it. Appeal to the conscience, not just the intellect.

label: Holy Spirit · the Spirit is a Person
title: Acts 13:2
text: "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them." First-person speech, a choice, authority. "Do actions have authority, or do persons?" / "He said 'I' and 'me' about Himself. That's self-awareness, right?"

label: Holy Spirit · the Spirit is a Person
title: Acts 15:28
text: "It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us." He takes part in a decision alongside the apostles. "Can a force agree with a council?"

label: Holy Spirit · the Spirit is a Person
title: Heb 3:7
text: "As the Holy Spirit says…" "Can energy speak to people?"

label: Holy Spirit · the Spirit is a Person
title: Eph 4:30; Isa 63:10; Ps 78:40
text: He can be grieved and rebelled against. "An active force can't be offended. Whoever the Spirit is, He's someone you can offend."

label: Holy Spirit · the Spirit is a Person
title: John 16:13
text: He "does not speak on His own; whatever He hears He speaks." (vs. Oneness or "Spirit = the Father") "Who is the Father hearing from?"

label: Holy Spirit · the Spirit is a Person
title: 1 Cor 1:24
text: Christ is called "the power of God." "Christ is called God's power and He's a person. So being God's power doesn't rule out being a person, right?"

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: 2 Sam 23:2–3: "The Spirit of Yahweh speaks by me… the God of Israel has said"
text: Acts 4:24–25: the "Sovereign Lord… who by the Holy Spirit, through the mouth of David" Go-to question: "So the Sovereign Lord who spoke through David is who?"

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: Ps 95:7–11: "They tested Me… I swore in My wrath" (Yahweh speaking)
text: Heb 3:7–11: "As the Holy Spirit says… they tested Me… I swore in My wrath" "Who is the Spirit talking about when He says 'they provoked Me'?"

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: Isa 6:8–10: the voice of the Lord (Yahweh of hosts, v.3–5) says "Go, and say to this people…"
text: Acts 28:25–26: "The Holy Spirit was right in saying to your fathers through Isaiah, 'Go to this people…'" Also John 12:41: Isaiah saw Christ's glory. One vision, three Persons.

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: Jer 31:31–34: "This is the covenant I will make… declares Yahweh"
text: Heb 10:15–17: "The Holy Spirit also bears witness… 'This is the covenant I will make'" The Spirit speaks Yahweh's covenant in the first person.

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: Ex 17:7: Israel "tested Yahweh"
text: Heb 3:7–9 (above) Same event.

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: Acts 5:3–4: "lie to the Holy Spirit" = "you have not lied to men but to God"
text: One-verse version.

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: Rom 8:9; 1 Pet 1:10–11
text: The Spirit is the "Spirit of God" and the "Spirit of Christ" If the Spirit is Yahweh's own Spirit and also Christ's…

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "That's personification."
text: "I didn't ask about figurative language. Can He speak, yes or no? If I say 'my car told me it's not starting today,' did my car speak?". Then: personified wisdom never chooses missionaries in real time (Acts 13:2).

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "He just communicates information / He has no mouth."
text: "Does the Father have a mouth? Does the Father speak?"

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "The Father told the Spirit to say it."
text: The text says "for me… I have called." That's not quoting someone else.

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "He's rational energy, like AI."
text: AI is programmed. The Spirit wills, commands and is provoked. "Can energy be rational without personhood?"

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "God used the Spirit's power to create."
text: God also created through Christ (John 1:3), and Christ is a person.

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "The 'Spirit of Yahweh' means 'from Yahweh,' not 'is Yahweh.'"
text: "The answer is yes to all of them." From Yahweh, and also Yahweh. Not either/or. Then: "He's also the Spirit of Christ, right?" (Rom 8:9). If they deny it, read the verse.

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "OK, so the Spirit is just the Father."
text: John 16:13 (He hears from another), John 14:16 (another Helper whom the Father sends). "Then the Father sends Himself and listens to Himself?"

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: They admit it but walk away from the Bible ("then I can't trust the Bible")
text: that's 2 Tim 4:3, "itching ears." They are conceding the Bible teaches it.

label: Method
title: Phase 1 = agree on the plain text. Nothing else moves until they do.
text: Read the verse and ask a yes/no question about what it says (not what it means). Don't go on until they answer. "I'm not moving to Phase 2 until you answer Phase 1."

label: Method
title: Yes/no questions, one at a time.
text: "Does the Holy Spirit speak? Yes or no?" Short questions are hard to wriggle out of. Long statements give them room to filibuster.

label: Method
title: Call out the dodge out loud.
text: When they redefine a word ("personification," "communicates information," "a vibe"), name it: "I didn't ask about personification. I asked, can He speak?"

label: Method
title: Use their rule on another verse.
text: When they invent a rule for one verse (e.g. "no article = 'a god'"), apply the same rule somewhere it obviously fails (John 1:6 becomes "a man sent from a god named a John").

label: Method
title: Hold them to their own analogy.
text: If they bring an analogy (king and messenger, software coder, three judges), don't swap it out. Push it until it proves your point: "Can the agent of the king claim to BE the king?"

label: Method
title: No topic-hopping.
text: When a point lands, people often jump to "Is Jesus God?" or "the Trinity makes no sense." Don't follow. "Let's finish this one first, then I'm happy to go there."

label: Method
title: Name the goalpost shift.
text: "First you wanted a Bible verse. I gave you the verse. Now it has to come from Jesus' own mouth?"

label: Method
title: "What's the only thing we do? Read."
text: When they say "context," make them show the verse in the context. Then wait. Silence works for you.

label: Method
title: Ask the question back.
text: End with a question they have to answer on their own ("Who is the Father hearing from?"), not a speech.

label: Method
title: Stay warm.
text: Even when they get angry or walk away: "I want you to be saved, brother. I love you." Truth with love keeps the door open (1 Pet 3:15–16).

label: Method · universal tool
title: "Yahweh" isn't one-person-only.
text: Yahweh is the name of the one true God, and Scripture applies it to the Father, the Son and the Spirit. Their "then Jesus is his own Father" syllogism only works if Yahweh = the Father alone. A name can have more than one referent: "Judah" can mean a man or a tribe (Judges 1:1–2).

label: Method · universal tool
title: Word–concept fallacy.
text: "'Trinity' isn't in the Bible" → neither are "monotheism" or "Bible." The question is whether the concept is there.

label: Method · universal tool
title: Three in one way, one in another.
text: Not a contradiction. Different categories: 3 persons, 1 being. (With a Muslim: the Quran comes in several transmitted readings, such as Hafs, Warsh and Qalun, and Muslims still say it is one Quran.)

label: Method · universal tool
title: Context decides literal vs. figurative.
text: Both sides agree personification exists. But personified things don't say "set apart for me" or "the work I have called them to."

label: Method · universal tool
title: "Firstborn" = rank, not birth order.
text: David was the youngest son and the second king, yet God calls him "firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth" (Ps 89:27).

label: For any conversation
title: The Gospel
text: Every conversation is headed here. Winning the argument saves no one. Christ does. Say the whole message plainly, call for a response, and leave the results to God.

label: The Gospel · Before you speak
title: God saves; you are faithful
text: your job is to say the truth clearly. God gives the growth. (1 Cor 3:6–7; Rom 1:16; John 6:44)

label: The Gospel · Before you speak
title: Law before grace
text: a person has to see their sin and God's judgment before the cross makes sense to them. (Rom 3:19–20; Gal 3:24)

label: The Gospel · Before you speak
title: Jesus is Lord
text: the call is to repent and follow Christ, not to repeat a prayer or add Jesus to a life that stays the same. (Luke 9:23; Rom 10:9; Acts 20:21)

label: The Gospel · Before you speak
title: No false promises
text: the gospel offers forgiveness and Christ Himself, not health, wealth or an easier life. (Phil 3:8; Mark 8:36; 2 Tim 3:12)

label: The Gospel
title: God is holy
text: God created all things and made us for Himself. He is holy and just, He cannot overlook sin, and He will judge every person. (Gen 1:1; Isa 6:3; Hab 1:13; Acts 17:24–31; Heb 9:27) "What do you think happens after we die?"

label: The Gospel
title: We are sinners under judgment
text: Every one of us has broken God's law. We are not basically good people who slip up; we are dead in sin, and the wages of sin is death. No amount of good works can pay it off. (Rom 3:10–12; Rom 3:23; Rom 6:23; Eph 2:1–3; Isa 64:6) "Have you kept God's law perfectly?"

label: The Gospel
title: Christ died and rose
text: God the Son became man, lived the sinless life we have not lived, and died in the place of sinners, bearing the wrath they deserve. He was buried, rose bodily on the third day, and is Lord of all. (John 1:14; Isa 53:5–6; 2 Cor 5:21; 1 Pet 3:18; Rom 5:8; 1 Cor 15:3–4; Phil 2:9–11) Only God can redeem a soul, and only a man can die in man's place, so the Savior is both. (Ps 49:7–9; Ps 49:15; 1 Tim 2:5–6; Heb 2:14–17) "Why did Jesus have to die?"

label: The Gospel
title: Repent and believe
text: God commands all people everywhere to repent. Whoever turns from sin and trusts in Christ alone is forgiven and has eternal life: by grace, through faith, not by works. Following Him costs everything, and no one who comes to Him is turned away. (Mark 1:15; Acts 17:30; John 3:16; Eph 2:8–9; Rom 10:9–13; Luke 14:27–28; John 6:37) "What is keeping you from turning to Christ today?"

label: The Gospel
title: The short version: the Romans Road
text: When you only have a minute, walk these in order, and call them to repent. (Rom 3:23; Rom 6:23; Rom 5:8; Acts 17:30; Rom 10:9–10; Rom 10:13; Rom 8:1)

label: The Gospel
title: How to walk someone through it
text: For a step-by-step way to do this in a real conversation, using the Ten Commandments first and then the cross, open The Way of the Master.

label: The Gospel
title: If they respond
text: Pray with them. Get them a Bible and get them into a church that preaches it, where they can be baptized by immersion as a believer. Follow up. Don't pronounce them saved. Point them to Christ, and let assurance grow from following Him. (Acts 2:41–42; Matt 28:19–20; 2 Cor 13:5; 1 John 2:3–6; John 8:31)

label: The Gospel
title: If they don't
text: Stay warm and leave the door open. You plant and water; God gives the growth. (1 Cor 3:6–7; 1 Pet 3:15–16; 2 Tim 2:24–26)

label: For any conversation
title: The Way of the Master
text: Use the law to reach the conscience, then give the gospel. God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble (James 4:6), so: law to the proud, grace to the humble. The Ten Commandments work like a mirror: they show a person their sin so that the cross makes sense. Jesus did this with the rich young ruler. (Rom 3:19–20; Rom 7:7; Gal 3:24; Mark 10:17–22)

label: The Way of the Master
title: 1. Start with an everyday question
text: Move from ordinary talk to spiritual things with one question. "What do you think happens after we die?"

label: The Way of the Master
title: 2. Are you a good person?
text: Almost everyone says yes. Let them say it. (Prov 20:6) "Would you consider yourself a good person?"

label: The Way of the Master
title: 3. Have you kept the Ten Commandments?
text: Walk through a few, one at a time, and let them answer each. (Ex 20:1–17) "Have you ever told a lie? What does that make you?" "Have you ever taken anything that wasn't yours, whatever its value?" "Have you ever used God's name as a curse word?" Jesus said that looking with lust is adultery in the heart. "Have you ever done that?" (Matt 5:27–28) Jesus put anger under the command "You shall not murder" (Matt 5:21–22), and John says whoever hates his brother is a murderer (1 John 3:15).

label: The Way of the Master
title: 4. Judgment: innocent or guilty?
text: Sum up what they admitted in their own words, then ask. (Heb 9:27; Rom 2:15–16; James 2:10) "If God judges you by that standard, will you be innocent or guilty?"

label: The Way of the Master
title: 5. Destiny: heaven or hell?
text: Don't soften it, and don't gloat. Say it because you care where they end up. (Rev 21:8; 1 Cor 6:9–10) "Would that be heaven or hell? Does that concern you?"

label: The Way of the Master
title: 6. Now give the good news
text: You stand guilty in God's courtroom, and Someone steps in and pays your fine in full. That is what Christ did on the cross, and He rose from the dead. (Rom 5:8; 2 Cor 5:21; 1 Pet 2:24; 1 Cor 15:3–4)

label: The Way of the Master
title: 7. Repent and trust
text: Believing a parachute exists won't save you; you have to put it on. Turn from sin and put your trust in Christ alone, today. (Acts 3:19; Acts 20:21; Rom 13:14; 2 Cor 6:2) "When are you going to do that?"

label: The Way of the Master
title: Keep in mind
text: Already humble? If someone is broken over their sin, skip the law and go straight to grace. answering objections clears the path, but the law and the gospel do the work. Don't spend an hour on arguments and never get here. (Rom 2:15) kind, patient, and plainly concerned for them. (2 Tim 2:24–26) Then go back to The Gospel for the full message and what to do when they respond.

label: For any conversation
title: Worldviews: how do you know?
text: Everyone starts somewhere. Only God's word gives you ground to stand on. A presupposition is what a person takes for granted before the argument starts. The atheist is not neutral, and neither are you. He already knows God and suppresses that truth (Rom 1:18–21), so you are not handing him a God he has never met. You are showing him that he leans on God every time he reasons, judges or trusts his own mind. (Prov 1:7; Col 2:3; Ps 14:1; 1 Cor 1:20)

label: Worldviews: how do you know?
title: What you are showing
text: You are not saying he knows nothing or believes in nothing. He reasons, does science and knows right from wrong, because he lives in God's world and is made in God's image. You are saying his worldview cannot account for any of it, and yours can. He is using the tools God gave him to argue against God. "We both use reason. I'm not asking whether you reason. I'm asking why reason can be trusted if your view is true."

label: Worldviews: how do you know?
title: Step 1: Don't give up your ground
text: Do not agree to set the Bible aside and argue from "neutral" facts. No one is neutral, and Scripture is the standard, not the thing on trial. You start from what God has revealed. He starts from his own guess. (Prov 26:4; 2 Cor 10:5; 1 Pet 3:15) "Would you set aside your trust in reason to prove reason? Then why should I set aside God's word?"

label: Worldviews: how do you know?
title: Step 2: Ask what he would accept
text: Before you give evidence, find out what he counts as evidence. If he has no standard, he has no basis for saying there isn't any. "What would count as evidence for you?" "Only what can be measured or tested." → "Did you measure that? Which experiment showed that only tested things are true?" That rule is not something the five senses can find. "I don't know what would convince me." → "Then how do you know there's no evidence?" "God is outside the universe, so He can't be tested." → Evidence is more than lab results. We reason, weigh testimony and draw conclusions every day. (Acts 1:3; Heb 11:1)

label: Worldviews: how do you know?
title: Step 3: Step into his view and show it cannot stand
text: Take his view on its own terms and ask what follows. One question at a time, and wait for the answer. (Prov 26:5) "How do you know that? How do you know anything for certain?" If he says we can't know anything for certain: "Are you certain of that?" "Are the laws of logic made of matter? Do they change? Where do unchanging, universal laws come from in a universe of matter in motion?" If he says God is illogical: "That assumes logic is reliable. In your view, where does it come from?" "You said 'mind.' Is that anything more than brain chemistry? If your thoughts are chemistry shaped for survival, why trust them to tell you what is true?" "Why expect nature to act tomorrow the way it did today?" (Gen 8:22; Col 1:17; Heb 1:3) "If we came from nothing and go to nothing, on what basis does anything you do matter?" If he says nothing has meaning: "Does that sentence have meaning?" (Eccl 1:2; Eccl 12:13–14)

label: Worldviews: how do you know?
title: Right and wrong
text: Start here when he calls something evil, unfair or hateful. "Is morality objective, or is it opinion?" "It's subjective." → "Then you can't say I'm wrong. You can only say you prefer something else, the way one person prefers burgers and another pizza." Watch for him to keep saying you are wrong anyway. Point it out kindly. "It comes from my experience." → "Someone raised to hate his neighbors has experience too. Is his hatred good?" Experience differs from person to person, so it cannot be the standard. "It comes from science." → Science tells you what is. It cannot tell you what ought to be. "Which experiment shows that lying is wrong?" "That's just your interpretation of the Bible." → Everyone interprets something: he interprets data and his own experience. Disagreement does not cancel truth. "If someone says 1 + 1 = 3, does that make the answer uncertain?" "That's true for you. This is my truth." → An opinion is not the same as truth. Truth is what matches reality, whoever believes it. "Can a person sincerely believe something and be wrong?" "It's objective." → "Then who set the standard, and why does it bind everyone?" (Rom 2:14–15)

label: Worldviews: how do you know?
title: Start with the Creator
text: Many people today have no Bible background. Words like sin, judgment and Savior mean little to someone who thinks he is an accident. Peter preached to people who knew the Scriptures and went straight to Christ and repentance (Acts 2:22–38). Paul, in Athens, began with the God who made the world and everything in it, and then said God now commands all people everywhere to repent (Acts 17:24–31). John's Gospel begins the same way: all things came into being through Christ (John 1:1–3; Col 1:16). You are not delaying the gospel. You are telling him whose world this is, so that sin makes sense and the cross is good news. "Who made you? And if you were made, who do you answer to?" Made on purpose. He is not a cosmic accident. He was made by God, in God's image, to know Him. (Gen 1:27; Ps 100:3; Ps 139:13–14) Worth. Every person bears God's image: unborn, disabled, old, unable to contribute anything. "If worth depends on what a person can do, is a strong man worth more than a child with Down syndrome?" (Gen 9:6; James 3:9) Guilt. He may have been taught that guilt is only herd instinct or upbringing. "When someone wrongs you, is that only instinct, or did he really do wrong?" The conscience is God's law written on the heart. (Rom 2:14–15) Then sin and the Savior. The One who made him is the One he has sinned against, and the One who came to die for sinners. (Col 1:16; Col 1:19–20)

label: Worldviews: how do you know?
title: Step 4: Bring him back to your ground
text: Show that what he has been borrowing belongs to God. Logic reflects God's unchanging mind, morality His holy character, the order of nature His faithfulness, and our reasoning His image in us. All things were made through the Word. (Gen 1:27; Mal 3:6; John 1:1–3; Acts 17:24–28)

label: Worldviews: how do you know?
title: If he says
text: "So you're saying atheists can't know anything?" → No. He knows a great deal. The question is whether his worldview can explain how. "I just lack belief. I don't have to prove anything." → "You still reason, judge and trust your mind every day. What do those rest on?" "That's circular. You're using God to prove God." → Every final starting point has to vouch for itself, or it isn't final. "Can you prove your words have meaning without using words?" The question is which starting point makes sense of everything else. His explains nothing. God's word explains logic, morality, science and him. (Heb 6:13) "We both just assume our senses work." → For him the senses are the foundation, with nothing under them. For you they are a tool, and under them is the God who made eyes, minds and the world they fit. "Logic is just a fact of the universe." → That repeats the claim; it doesn't explain it. "Would you accept it if I said God is just a fact of the universe?" "Logic is just how humans think." → Then it could have been otherwise, and it would not bind anyone who thinks differently, including you. "Morality comes from evolution or society." → That tells you what people do approve of, not what they ought to. Was slavery right when society approved it? "I don't know where they come from, and that's fine." → "So you rely on them with no reason to. That is faith. I can tell you where they come from."

label: Worldviews: how do you know?
title: Watch out
text: Don't say "you believe in nothing." He will name things he believes, and he'll be right. Say his worldview can't account for them. Don't call him or his view dumb, and don't dismiss him. Say "that doesn't hold together," and stay kind when he gets sharp. (2 Tim 2:24–26) Don't blame evil on God's hands being tied. When evil or hell comes up, don't say God wanted to stop it but free will prevented Him. God is sovereign over all things, He is not the author of sin, and people answer for their own sin. Use the evil and suffering answer and the "why create me?" answer. (Eph 1:11; Gen 50:20; Acts 2:23) Don't trade away creation to sound reasonable. God made everything in six days. See the evolution answer. The full case is on The fallacy of evolution. Don't treat it as a trick. Winning the exchange saves no one. He is not confused; he is suppressing the truth, and only God opens blind eyes. (2 Cor 4:4–6; 1 Cor 2:14) Evidence still belongs. The apostles pointed to the empty tomb and the eyewitnesses. Give the evidence as God's facts, not as something a neutral judge gets to rule on. (Acts 17:31; 1 Cor 15:3–8) Don't lean on quotes and numbers you can't back up. A line credited to Darwin or a statistic from a sermon can be wrong, and one bad quote costs you the hearing. Stay with Scripture and with questions. Get to the cross. This clears the ground. Then give The Gospel. For a short version to run live, open the borrowed capital play.

label: For any conversation
title: The problem of evil
text: Why does a good God allow suffering? This is the question behind most unbelief, and often it is not an argument but a wound. Find out which before you answer. Scripture does not explain every sorrow. It tells us who rules over suffering, where it came from, what God has done about it, and how it ends. (Deut 29:29; Rom 8:28)

label: The problem of evil
title: First, listen
text: "Is this a question you're thinking through, or something you're living through?" If he is hurting, sit with him before you reason with him. Job's friends did well for seven days, until they opened their mouths. Weep with those who weep. (Job 2:13; Rom 12:15; John 11:35)

label: The problem of evil
title: What you are showing
text: To call anything evil, he needs a real standard of good that stands above every person and culture. In a universe of matter and chance there is suffering, but there is no "ought not." The complaint itself borrows from the God it is aimed at. See Morality and justice. "When you say that's evil, do you mean you dislike it, or that it is really wrong? By what standard?"

label: The problem of evil
title: What Scripture says
text: God made the world very good. Evil is not part of what He made. (Gen 1:31) Sin brought death and suffering in. Man rebelled, and the whole creation was subjected to futility. (Gen 3:17–19; Rom 5:12; Rom 8:20–22) God is sovereign over all of it, and He is not the author of sin. Nothing happens outside His rule, and He tempts no one. (Eph 1:11; Isa 45:7; James 1:13; 1 John 1:5) He means for good what men mean for evil. Joseph's brothers sold him; God sent him to save lives. (Gen 50:20; Rom 8:28) The cross is the clearest case. The worst evil ever done, the murder of the Son of God, was carried out by lawless men and was God's predetermined plan to save sinners. If God can bring the greatest good out of the greatest evil, He can be trusted with the rest. (Acts 2:23; Acts 4:27–28) He does not owe us an account. When Job asked why, God answered with Himself. (Job 38:1–4; Job 42:1–6; Rom 9:20) He entered it. Our God is not far off from pain. He became a man of sorrows. (Isa 53:3–5; Heb 4:15) He will end it. Every wrong will be judged, and every tear wiped away. (Rev 21:3–4; Acts 17:31; Rom 8:18)

label: The problem of evil
title: If they say
text: "A good God would stop evil." → He will, and on a set day. The harder question is what happens to us when He does, since the evil is not only out there. He waits because He is patient. (2 Pet 3:9; Rom 2:4) "If God removed all evil at midnight tonight, where would that leave you and me?" "Why doesn't He stop it now?" → We are not told every reason, and a God big enough to blame is big enough to have reasons we cannot see. What we are told is that He is working all things together for good for those who love Him. (Rom 8:28; Isa 55:8–9) "What about natural disasters and disease?" → They belong to a creation that groans under the curse, and Jesus says they are a call to repent, not proof that the victims were worse than we are. (Rom 8:20–22; Luke 13:1–5) "What about children who suffer?" → Do not hurry this one. God is the defender of the helpless and will judge every hand raised against a child. Our own outrage is His image in us. (Ps 10:14; Matt 18:6; Gen 18:25) "I prayed and He didn't answer." → Paul prayed three times, and Christ prayed in Gethsemane. The answer was grace to bear it, and then resurrection. (2 Cor 12:8–9; Matt 26:39) "Then God is the cause of evil." → No. Men do evil from their own hearts and are fully responsible for it. God rules over it for holy ends without doing it. Scripture holds both together in one sentence. (Acts 2:23; James 1:13–14)

label: The problem of evil
title: Watch out
text: Don't say God's hands were tied by our free will. He is never helpless. Say He is sovereign and good, and that He has purposes. Don't explain a particular tragedy. You do not know why this child died or that cancer came. Say so. (Deut 29:29) Don't answer a wound with an argument. Know which one is in front of you. Don't leave out the cross. It is the only place the problem of evil is answered and not only discussed.

label: The problem of evil
title: Bring it to the gospel
text: The real question is not why bad things happen to good people. There was only one good Person, and He volunteered. He suffered for sinners so that suffering would not have the last word over them. (1 Pet 3:18; 2 Cor 5:21; Rom 8:32) "God did something about evil at the cross. Have you ever looked at what He did there for you?" Then give The Gospel.

label: For any conversation
title: Morality and justice
text: Can morality exist without God? Everyone you meet believes some things are really wrong. Your aim is to show that only the God of Scripture makes sense of that, and that the same God who gives the law will judge by it. (Rom 2:14–16; Acts 17:31)

label: Morality and justice
title: What you are showing
text: You are not saying an unbeliever cannot be kind, honest or brave. He can, because he is made in God's image and God's law is written on his heart. You are saying he cannot account for right and wrong. He can know it, and he cannot explain why it binds anyone. (Rom 2:14–15; Gen 1:27) "Is anything wrong for everyone, everywhere, whether they agree or not? What makes it so?"

label: Morality and justice
title: Where the standard comes from
text: Good is what God is. He does not look up to a standard above Him, and He does not invent it on a whim. Righteousness and justice are the foundation of His throne. (Ps 89:14; Deut 32:4; 1 John 1:5) He has told us. What is good is not a mystery. (Mic 6:8; Ex 20:1–17; Matt 22:37–40) It is written on every heart. That is why cultures everywhere punish murder, theft and betrayal. (Rom 2:14–15) People matter because God made them. Human worth does not come from usefulness or strength. (Gen 9:6; James 3:9)

label: Morality and justice
title: Why the other answers fail
text: "Each person decides." → Then no one is ever wrong, including the man who robs him. He will not live by that. Press it to the end: if right and wrong come from the individual, "my truth," then the rapist is never wrong, because he was acting on his. "Was he wrong, or only different from you?" "Society decides." → Then the reformer is always the villain. Slavery was legal, and the people who opposed it were breaking society's rules. "Was slavery right when most people approved of it?" And if a society's agreement is what makes a thing good, then what Hitler's Germany did to the Jews was good, there and then, for them. Nobody believes that. At Nuremberg the judges did not accept "our laws allowed it"; they held those men to a law above every nation. "Whose law was that?" "Evolution gave us morals." → That would explain why we feel them, not why we must obey them. Survival also rewards cruelty and deceit. "Whatever reduces suffering." → Why should anyone care about a stranger's suffering? That is already a moral rule, and it needs a source. "Science tells us." → Science describes what is. It cannot tell you what ought to be. "Is it good because God commands it, or does He command it because it's good?" → Neither. It is good because it reflects who He is, and His nature does not change. (Mal 3:6; James 1:17)

label: Morality and justice
title: Justice needs a Judge
text: Most wrongs are never put right in this life. Killers die in their beds. If death ends everything, justice is a wish. (Eccl 8:14; Ps 73:3–17) God will bring every act into judgment. That is good news for every victim. (Eccl 12:14; Rom 2:5–6; Rev 20:11–13) It is hard news for all of us. The standard we use on others will be used on us, and none of us has kept even our own. (Rom 2:1; Rom 3:19; Rom 3:23) "You want justice done. Do you want it done to you?"

label: Morality and justice
title: If they say
text: "I don't need God to be good." → Agreed that you can do good things. Good by whose measure? And have you done all the good you know? (James 4:17) "Religious people do terrible things." → Yes, and you can only call them terrible if there is a standard they broke. Christianity gives you the grounds to condemn its own hypocrites. (Matt 7:21–23) "The God of the Old Testament commanded terrible things." → To judge God you need a standard above Him. Where does it come from? Then open the text: the Judge of all the earth does right, and He is patient for centuries before He judges. (Gen 18:25; Gen 15:16) "Morality is just empathy." → Empathy is a feeling, and feelings differ. Some feel none. "Is cruelty wrong for the man who feels nothing?"

label: Morality and justice
title: Bring it to the gospel
text: At the cross God did not set justice aside to show mercy. He satisfied it. Christ bore the penalty, so that God is both just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus. (Rom 3:25–26; Isa 53:5–6; 1 John 1:9) "If God judged you by your own standard, how would you do? Would you like to know how a guilty person can be declared right?" Then give The Gospel. For the way of arguing behind this page, see Worldviews.

label: For any conversation
title: The exclusivity of Christ
text: Why is Jesus the only way? We did not make this claim. Jesus did. The question is never whether Christians are narrow. It is whether what He said is true. (John 14:6; Acts 4:12)

label: The exclusivity of Christ
title: What you are showing
text: Every view of God shuts some views out. The man who says all religions lead to God is telling the Muslim, the Hindu and the Christian that each is wrong about his own faith. There is no neutral, wider place to stand. So ask which claim is true. "When you say all paths lead to God, how do you know that? And doesn't that say every religion is wrong where it disagrees with you?"

label: The exclusivity of Christ
title: What Jesus and the apostles said
text: "I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father but through Me." (John 14:6) No other name. (Acts 4:12) One God, one Mediator. (1 Tim 2:5–6) Whoever has the Son has life. (John 3:36; 1 John 5:11–12) The Old Testament says the same of God. "There is no savior besides Me." (Isa 43:11; Isa 45:22)

label: The exclusivity of Christ
title: Why there can be only one
text: Because of what the problem is. We are not lost for lack of advice. We are guilty before a holy God. Guilt needs a payment, not a path. (Rom 3:23; Rom 6:23) Because of who can pay. Only one who is truly man can stand in for men, and only one who is truly God can bear it. No one else is both. (Heb 2:17; Col 2:9; Ps 49:7–8) Because of what the cross means. If there were another way, the Father would have taken it. Christ asked in the garden. (Matt 26:39; Gal 2:21) Because He rose. No other founder left an empty tomb. God gave proof to everyone by raising Him. (Acts 17:31; Rom 1:4)

label: The exclusivity of Christ
title: The religions do not agree
text: They cannot all be true, because they contradict each other on the very things that matter: who God is, who Jesus is, and how a sinner is made right. Every other religion says do. The gospel says done. (Eph 2:8–9; John 19:30)

label: The exclusivity of Christ
title: If they say
text: "That's arrogant." → It would be, if we were the way. We are beggars telling other beggars where the bread is. Arrogance is deciding for God how He must save. (1 Cor 4:7; Titus 3:5) "What about people who never heard?" → No one is condemned for not hearing. Men are condemned for sin against the light they have: creation and conscience. That is why we go. (Rom 1:18–20; Rom 2:12–16; Rom 10:13–15) "You have heard. What will you do with it?" "Sincere people in other religions will be fine." → Sincerity does not change what is true. A man can sincerely take the wrong medicine. (Prov 14:12; Rom 10:1–3) "What about the billions who sincerely live good lives in their own faith?" → A lifelong Catholic of seventy-five asked John MacArthur exactly this. His answer: they perish, because there is salvation in no other name, and no one is good before God. The degree of punishment differs with the light a person rejected, not with how good he was. Then MacArthur turned it on the man himself: knowing the facts about Christ is not enough either; "you must trust Christ for your salvation alone," and no Masses, confessions or rosaries add to it. The man said he was leaving the Catholic church. [MacArthur, Q&A at Grace Community Church] (Acts 4:12; John 8:24; Luke 18:19; Matt 7:21–23; Rom 3:20) "All religions teach basically the same thing." → On ethics there is overlap. On God and salvation they are opposites. Ask him to name what Islam, Hinduism and Christianity each say about Jesus. "It's exclusive, so it's intolerant." → The way is narrow, and the invitation is as wide as the world. "Whoever will call on the name of the Lord will be saved." (Matt 7:13–14; Rom 10:13; John 6:37; Rev 22:17) "That's true for you." → Jesus did not say He was a way for some. He rose in public history, or He did not.

label: The exclusivity of Christ
title: Bring it to the gospel
text: The only way is an open way. He turns away no one who comes. (John 6:37; Matt 11:28; Isa 55:1) "If He is the only way to the Father, are you on it?" Then give The Gospel.

label: For any conversation
title: The resurrection
text: Historical evidence that Jesus rose from the dead. Christianity stands or falls here, and Paul says so. If Christ has not been raised, our faith is worthless. He has been raised, and God has given proof of it to everyone. Give the evidence as God's facts, not as an exhibit for a neutral judge. (1 Cor 15:14; 1 Cor 15:17; Acts 17:31)

label: The resurrection
title: What you are showing
text: The resurrection was preached in the city where it happened, within weeks, in front of the people who had killed Him and could have produced the body. It was not a legend that grew far away over centuries. (Acts 2:22–24; Acts 2:32; Acts 26:26) "If Jesus really rose from the dead, would you follow Him? If not, is evidence really the issue?"

label: The resurrection
title: The facts to account for
text: He died. Roman soldiers knew when a man was dead, and a spear confirmed it. (John 19:33–35; Mark 15:44–45) He was buried in a known tomb, belonging to a member of the council. (Mark 15:43–46) The tomb was empty on the third day. The authorities never denied it. They explained it by saying the body was stolen. (Matt 28:11–15) Women found it first. No one inventing the story in that world would have chosen witnesses the courts did not accept. (Luke 24:1–11; John 20:1–2) He appeared to many, over forty days. To individuals, to groups, to more than five hundred at once, most of them still alive when Paul wrote. They ate with Him and touched Him. (1 Cor 15:3–8; Luke 24:36–43; Acts 1:3) The witnesses were changed. Men who ran and hid went out and preached it, and suffered for it. People die for what they believe is true. No one dies for what he knows he made up. (Acts 4:18–20; Acts 5:40–42) Enemies believed. James, who had not believed in his brother, and Saul, who was hunting Christians, each said he saw the risen Christ. (John 7:5; 1 Cor 15:7–8; Gal 1:13–16) It was foretold. (Ps 16:10; Isa 53:10–11; Matt 16:21)

label: The resurrection
title: The summary Paul received
text: The statement in 1 Corinthians 15:3–5 is one Paul says he was handed. He met Peter and James in Jerusalem within a few years of the cross. This is testimony from the beginning, from the men who were there. (1 Cor 15:3–5; Gal 1:18–19)

label: The resurrection
title: If they say
text: "The disciples stole the body." → Then they suffered and died for what they knew was a fraud, and not one of them broke. And the guards' story is "we were asleep, and we saw who did it." (Matt 28:11–15) "He didn't really die." → A man scourged, crucified and speared does not roll a stone, overpower guards and convince anyone he is the Lord of life. (John 19:33–34) "They hallucinated." → Groups do not share one hallucination, and not over forty days in different places. And the tomb would still hold the body. (1 Cor 15:6; Luke 24:39–43) "They went to the wrong tomb." → Then the authorities only had to go to the right one. "It's a legend that grew later." → The claim is in the earliest sources, in the names of living witnesses, in the city where it happened. (1 Cor 15:3–8; Luke 1:1–4) "Dead men don't rise. Miracles are impossible." → No one says men rise by nature. The claim is that God raised Him. That is only impossible if there is no God, which is the very thing in question. (Acts 26:8; Jer 32:17) "The Gospels contradict each other." → Witnesses who agree on the event and differ in what they include are what honest testimony looks like. See Is the Bible reliable?

label: The resurrection
title: Watch out
text: Evidence does not raise the dead. Men saw Lazarus walk out and plotted to kill him. If they do not hear Moses and the Prophets, they will not be persuaded if someone rises from the dead. Pray, and preach. (John 12:9–11; Luke 16:31) Don't argue "probably." The apostles announced it. (Acts 2:36) Don't stop at the fact. Say what it means.

label: The resurrection
title: What it means
text: Jesus is who He said He is. (Rom 1:4) The payment was accepted. He was raised for our justification. (Rom 4:25) Death is beaten. Those who are His will be raised. (1 Cor 15:20–22; John 11:25–26) His resurrection is not like Lazarus's. Lazarus came out still bound in his grave clothes and later died again. Jesus left His lying in the tomb and will never die again. Lazarus shows that Christ's voice commands death; Christ's own rising is the first of a new kind of life, the one His people will share. [Abner Chou, sermon on John 11:41–44] (John 11:43–44; John 20:6–7; Rom 6:9; 1 Cor 15:20) A day of judgment is fixed, and the Judge has been named. (Acts 17:30–31) "He is alive today. What will you do with a living Lord?" Then give The Gospel. For the short version to run live, open the resurrection play.

label: For any conversation
title: Hell and eternal judgment
text: Why would a loving God send people to hell? Speak about hell the way Jesus did: plainly, often, and with tears. He said more about it than anyone in Scripture, and He is the one who went to the cross to save people from it. (Matt 10:28; Luke 19:41; Matt 23:37)

label: Hell and eternal judgment
title: What you are showing
text: The question assumes we are basically good people and God is overreacting. Scripture says the opposite about both. Once a man sees who God is and what sin is, the question changes from "How could God send anyone to hell?" to "How could God let anyone into heaven?" (Rom 3:10–12; Rom 3:23; Hab 1:13) "Do you think anything deserves judgment? Then who decides what, and how much?"

label: Hell and eternal judgment
title: What Scripture says
text: Hell is real, conscious and eternal. Jesus uses the same word for the punishment and for the life. (Matt 25:41; Matt 25:46; Rev 14:11; Rev 20:10) It is judgment, not an accident. It is the just sentence of a holy Judge on real guilt. (Rev 20:11–15; Rom 2:5–6; 2 Thess 1:8–9) It is fair. God judges each one according to his deeds and according to the light he had. (Rom 2:6; Luke 12:47–48; Gen 18:25) No one is there who wanted Christ. Men love darkness and will not come to the light. (John 3:19–20; John 5:40) Being religious does not lessen it. Jesus said the scribes, the most religious men in Israel, "will receive greater condemnation." MacArthur on that verse: the idea that there is good in every religion runs straight into it, since those men believed in the God of Abraham and were judged more severely for a self-righteous system and for rejecting Christ. The worst judgment is for those who knew the most and trampled it. [MacArthur, sermon on Mark 12:38–44] (Mark 12:38–40; Matt 23:15; Heb 10:29; Luke 12:47–48) God takes no pleasure in it. (Ezek 33:11; 2 Pet 3:9) There is no second chance after death. (Heb 9:27; Luke 16:26)

label: Hell and eternal judgment
title: Why it is eternal
text: Because of who is sinned against. The weight of a wrong rises with the worth of the one wronged. Sin is against an infinitely holy God. (Ps 51:4; Isa 6:3–5) Because sinners there do not stop sinning. Hell does not make anyone repent. (Rev 16:9–11) Because the cross shows what sin costs. If sin were small, the Son of God would not have had to die for it. (Rom 8:32; Isa 53:10)

label: Hell and eternal judgment
title: If they say
text: "A loving God wouldn't do that." → A God who shrugged at rape and murder would not be loving. Love for victims requires justice. And His love is not a guess: He gave His Son. (Rom 5:8; John 3:16; Nah 1:3) "Eternal punishment for a few years of sin isn't fair." → Time spent sinning is not how we measure a crime. A murder takes a moment. And see "Why it is eternal" above. "I'm a good person." → By whose standard? Walk through the commandments. See The Way of the Master. (James 2:10; Rom 3:19–20) "God sends people to hell for not believing in Jesus." → People are condemned for their sin. Jesus is the rescue they refuse. A man does not die because he refused the doctor, but from the disease. (John 3:17–18; John 3:36) "What about those who never heard?" → See The exclusivity of Christ. (Rom 1:18–20) "Hell is just separation from God" / "the wicked are simply destroyed." → Jesus describes fire, darkness, weeping and a punishment as lasting as eternal life. (Matt 13:41–42; Matt 25:46; Mark 9:47–48) "I'd rather be in hell with my friends." → There is no friendship there. Every good thing you have ever enjoyed came from the God you would be without. (James 1:17; Luke 16:23–28)

label: Hell and eternal judgment
title: Watch out
text: Don't soften what Jesus said, and don't enjoy saying it. Paul warned people with tears. (Acts 20:31; Rom 9:1–3) Don't pronounce on a particular dead person. Say God will do right, and turn to the living man in front of you. (Gen 18:25) Don't use hell as a threat to win. It is a warning from someone who was headed there too. (Eph 2:3–5; 2 Cor 5:11) Don't leave him there. Hell is never the end of the conversation.

label: Hell and eternal judgment
title: Bring it to the gospel
text: On the cross Christ bore the wrath of God for sinners. Everyone's sin will be punished: either in hell, or in Him. That is why no one has to go. (Isa 53:5–6; Gal 3:13; 1 Thess 1:10; Rom 8:1) "He took what sinners deserve so they could go free. Will you turn from your sin and trust Him?" Then give The Gospel.

label: For any conversation
title: The end times
text: What is coming, and how to talk about it People bring this up on their own: a war, a headline about Israel, a funeral, a fear about where the world is going. Each one is an open door. Your aim is not to win a chart debate but to show that history is going where God said it would, that Christ is the King and Judge it ends with, and that today is the day to be ready. This page follows our church's position, premillennial and pretribulational, as Abner Chou and John MacArthur teach it. (Acts 17:30–31; 1 Pet 3:15; Titus 2:13)

label: The end times
title: How to read prophecy
text: The same way you read the rest. Chou: what God meant is what the text means, in normal language, by the ordinary rules of grammar and the facts of history. Men moved by the Holy Spirit spoke from God. (2 Pet 1:20–21; Luke 24:44) Words stay what they are. Israel is Israel and the church is the church, and just as much Egypt is Egypt and Assyria is Assyria. Isaiah says both of those old enemies will one day worship with Israel, so this is not favoritism toward one nation; it is God keeping every word to every nation. (Isa 19:23–25; Rom 11:28–29) Fulfilled prophecy sets the pattern. The promises about Christ's first coming came true literally: Bethlehem, a donkey, pierced hands, a rich man's tomb. Expect the rest to come true the same way. (Mic 5:2; Zech 9:9; Isa 53:9) It is clear, and it takes work. Chou compares it to calculus: not unclear, but it has many prerequisites, because the last things draw on the whole Bible. So be patient and humble with those still working through it.

label: The end times
title: Daniel's outline
text: The statue (Daniel 2). Four real empires in order: Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece, Rome. Then a stone not cut by hands strikes the statue and becomes a mountain that fills the earth. Chou's point: the stone, Christ, comes first and the kingdom follows, and since the four kingdoms were physical, so is the fifth. That is premillennialism in one chapter. (Dan 2:34–35; Dan 2:44–45) The seventy weeks (Daniel 9). Seventy sevens of years are decreed for Israel. From the decree to rebuild Jerusalem until Messiah the Prince is sixty-nine of them. After that the Messiah is cut off, and the city and the sanctuary are destroyed, which happened in AD 70. One seven remains: a ruler makes a firm covenant for one week and breaks it in the middle. That last seven is the seven-year tribulation. (Dan 9:24–27) Why it matters in conversation. Sixty-nine of the seventy came to pass on schedule, the crucifixion included. Chou: God got all of that right, so we can trust Him for the seventieth. See Jewish for using Daniel 9 with a Jewish friend. The Son of Man (Daniel 7). After the beast kingdoms, One like a Son of Man comes with the clouds and is given dominion over all peoples forever. Jesus took that title for Himself at His trial. (Dan 7:13–14; Mark 14:61–62)

label: The end times
title: The rapture, in three steps
text: From Abner Chou's message on the rapture. Every Christian believes in a rapture. Paul defines it as the dead in Christ rising and the living being changed and caught up. That is the resurrection, and the resurrection is part of the gospel. The only question is when. (1 Thess 4:13–18; 1 Cor 15:51–53) It is not the same event as the second coming. Ask who, where and how. When the prophets describe Israel's regathering, people travel home across the ground to Jerusalem. Paul says he is revealing something new, a mystery: the church is gathered in the air, by Christ Himself, and taken to be with Him. Different people, different place, different direction. (Deut 30:3–5; Isa 60:4, 9; 1 Thess 4:15–17; John 14:2–3) It comes before the tribulation. Paul ties the timing of the rapture to the start of the day of the Lord, which comes like a thief. Believers are delivered from the wrath to come. The Thessalonians panicked at the thought that the day of the Lord had begun, which only makes sense if they had been taught they would not be in it. Christ promises to keep His church from the hour of testing. And in Revelation the word "church" fills chapters 2 and 3, vanishes through the judgments of chapters 6 to 18, and reappears in heaven as the bride in chapter 19. (1 Thess 5:1–2; 1 Thess 1:10; 2 Thess 2:1–3; Rev 3:10; Rev 19:7–8) "If Christ called His people today, would you be among them?"

label: The end times
title: Why God planned it this way
text: Chou gives six purposes, each from the texts themselves. To keep His promises to Israel. With the church taken up, God turns again to Israel, as Revelation shows. (Rev 7:4; Rom 11:25–27) To prepare the church. Believers appear before the judgment seat of Christ and are made ready for the marriage supper of the Lamb. (2 Cor 5:10; Rev 19:7–9) To mark the last stage of His plan plainly. It is sudden, and it is announced with a trumpet. (1 Cor 15:52) To give hope. Death, grief and pain are not how the story ends for those in Christ. (1 Thess 4:13–14; Rom 8:18) To give perspective. The church will never face the worst. Whatever we suffer now is still grace, and better than we deserve. (1 Thess 5:9; 2 Cor 4:17) To keep us ready. It can happen at any moment, with nothing that must come first. Chou: "This isn't about escaping from this world. This is about escaping worldliness." (1 Thess 5:6–10; Titus 2:11–13; 1 John 3:2–3)

label: The end times
title: God is not finished with Israel
text: His promise stands as long as the sun and moon do. (Jer 31:35–37) There has always been a believing remnant inside the nation, and Paul was part of it. (Rom 11:1–5) A day is coming when the nation and the remnant are the same. Israel will look on the One they pierced and mourn, a fountain will be opened for sin, and all Israel will be saved. MacArthur preaches Isaiah 53 as the words Israel will say on that day, looking back: "He was pierced for our transgressions." (Zech 12:10; Zech 13:1; Rom 11:26; Isa 53:4–6) Their survival is itself evidence. MacArthur's question: have you ever met a Hittite or an Amorite? Israel is still here because God is not done. So the gospel still goes to the Jew first. (Rom 1:16; Rom 10:1)

label: The end times
title: The King and His kingdom
text: Christ returns in glory, visibly, to the earth. (Zech 14:4; Matt 24:29–30; Rev 19:11–16) He reigns a thousand years from Jerusalem, on David's throne, and the nations come to Him. Revelation gives the number six times in seven verses. (Rev 20:1–6; Isa 2:2–4; Luke 1:32–33) The honor is His alone. Chou: "Christ does not reign with us; we reign with him." The reason there must be a kingdom on this earth is that the last Adam must rule where the first Adam fell. (Dan 7:13–14; 1 Cor 15:22–25; Rom 5:17)

label: The end times
title: Judgment and the new creation
text: Every person will be raised and judged. Those not found in the book of life go to the lake of fire. See Hell and eternal judgment. (Rev 20:11–15; John 5:28–29; Dan 12:2) God makes all things new. A new heaven and a new earth, no more death or tears, and God dwelling with His people. (Rev 21:1–5; 2 Pet 3:10–13; Isa 65:17)

label: The end times
title: If they say
text: "Every generation has thought it was the end." → Peter said scoffers would say exactly that. The delay is not slowness; it is patience, giving people time to repent. Then the day comes like a thief. (2 Pet 3:3–4; 2 Pet 3:8–10) "People keep predicting dates and getting it wrong." → They do, and they are disobeying Jesus when they do it. No one knows the day or the hour. Chou's warning is against "newspaper theology": our footing is the text, not the headlines. (Matt 24:36; Acts 1:7) "The rapture was invented in the 1800s." → A doctrine being discussed more in one century does not mean it began then. Justification was not invented at the Reformation, or the deity of Christ at Nicaea. Chou points to Irenaeus in the second century speaking of the church being "caught up" before the tribulation [Irenaeus, Against Heresies 5.29.1]. In the end the question is what Paul wrote. (1 Thess 4:17; Acts 17:11) "The Bible hardly mentions it." → Once would be enough. And Paul says it was a mystery, not revealed before, so it appears only where the church's future is in view, and it appears there every time. (1 Cor 15:51; 1 Thess 4:15) "That is escapism. You just want out, so you do nothing." → Paul rebuked people who used the Lord's return as an excuse to quit working. Chou: knowing the King is coming is the reason for evangelism and holiness, not a reason to stop. (2 Thess 3:10–12; 1 Cor 15:58; Matt 24:45–46) "Revelation is all symbols." → It uses symbols, and it usually tells you what they stand for. Symbols point to real things. It also opens with a blessing on the one who reads and keeps it, which assumes it can be understood. (Rev 1:3; Rev 1:20; Rev 17:15) "The church has replaced Israel." → Paul asks, "Has God rejected His people?" and answers, "May it never be." The gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable. (Rom 11:1; Rom 11:28–29; Jer 31:35–37) "Christians can't even agree on this." → On the main things we do: Christ will return bodily, raise the dead, judge the world and make all things new. Brothers who order the events differently are still brothers, and Chou says he has learned from them. Don't let an in-house discussion keep you from the question that matters: are you ready to meet Him? (Acts 1:11; 2 Tim 4:1; Heb 9:27–28) "Is this it? Is what's happening in the news the end?" → No one can say that an event is the sign. What we can say is that nothing has to happen before Christ calls His church, and that the stage Scripture describes, Israel back in her land and the nations against her, is one no one expected for most of history. Be ready either way. (1 Thess 5:1–6; Zech 12:2–3; Luke 12:40)

label: The end times
title: Watch out
text: Never set a date, and don't pass along those who do. (Matt 24:36) Don't let the chart replace the Person. Chou on Revelation: "It's about the triune God." John was given it on what may have been the worst day of his life, and what he was shown first was Christ. (Rev 1:9–18) Don't make it a test of fellowship. The gospel is the line. A brother who is amillennial or postmillennial is a brother. Don't use it only to frighten. The same passages are written to comfort believers. (1 Thess 4:18; 1 Thess 5:11) Don't stop at the timeline. With an unbeliever the point is always the same: the Judge is coming, and He is also the Savior.

label: The end times
title: Bring it to the gospel
text: God has fixed a day on which He will judge the world in righteousness through a Man He has appointed, and He has given proof to everyone by raising Him from the dead. That Man first came to bear sin. He is coming a second time for salvation to those who eagerly wait for Him. The last invitation in the Bible is still open: let the one who is thirsty come. (Acts 17:30–31; Heb 9:27–28; 2 Cor 6:2; Rev 22:17; Rev 22:20) "If He came today, would you meet Him as your Savior or as your Judge?" Then give The Gospel. For the hope behind all of this, see The resurrection.

label: For any conversation
title: Faith and reason
text: Is believing in God irrational, or blind faith? Biblical faith is not belief without evidence, and it is not a leap in the dark. It is trust in a Person who has spoken and has proved Himself trustworthy. And reason is not faith's rival. It is a gift from the God the unbeliever is using it against. (Heb 11:1; Isa 1:18; Prov 1:7)

label: Faith and reason
title: What you are showing
text: Everyone trusts something he cannot prove first: his senses, his memory, his reason, the order of nature. The unbeliever has faith too. The question is not faith or reason. It is which faith makes reason possible. See Worldviews. "What do you trust that you can't prove? Why do you trust your own mind?"

label: Faith and reason
title: What faith is
text: Faith is trust in what God has said. Abraham was fully assured that what God had promised, He was able to do. (Rom 4:20–21; Heb 11:1; Heb 11:6) It rests on what God has done in public. The apostles appealed to what was seen, heard and touched, and said it was not done in a corner. (1 John 1:1–3; Luke 1:1–4; Acts 26:25–26; 2 Pet 1:16) It comes by hearing the word of Christ. (Rom 10:17; John 20:30–31) It is a gift. No one reasons himself into the kingdom. God opens blind eyes. (Eph 2:8–9; 2 Cor 4:4–6; 1 Cor 2:14)

label: Faith and reason
title: What reason is
text: God commands us to think. "Come now, and let us reason together." We are to love Him with all our mind. (Isa 1:18; Matt 22:37; Rom 12:2) The apostles reasoned. Paul reasoned from the Scriptures, explaining and giving evidence. We are told to be ready with a defense. (Acts 17:2–3; Acts 18:4; 1 Pet 3:15) Reason has a starting point. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge. All the treasures of wisdom are hidden in Christ. (Prov 1:7; Col 2:3; Ps 36:9) Reason is a tool, not the judge. It is used under God's word, and it is bent by sin like the rest of us. (Rom 1:21–22; 2 Cor 10:5; Eph 4:17–18)

label: Faith and reason
title: If they say
text: "Faith is believing without evidence." → That is not how the Bible uses the word. You have faith in your wife or your surgeon because of what you know of them. "Do you trust anyone you've never tested in a lab?" "I only believe what can be proven by science." → That sentence cannot be proven by science. And science itself runs on trust that nature is orderly and our minds can know it. (Gen 8:22; Col 1:17) "Science has replaced God." → Science explains how things in the world work. It does not explain why there is a world, why it is orderly, or why we can understand it. Modern science grew among men who expected order because they believed in a Lawgiver. "Smart people don't believe." → Many do, and always have. But truth is not settled by counting, and God chose what the world calls foolish to shame the wise. (1 Cor 1:20–27) "You believe because you were raised that way." → Where a belief came from does not tell you whether it is true. He was raised to believe things too. "Show me God and I'll believe." → He has shown Himself in what He made, in conscience, in Scripture, and in His Son. People saw Jesus raise the dead and still refused. (Rom 1:19–20; John 12:37; John 14:9) "If I can't understand it, I won't accept it." → He accepts many things he cannot fully understand. And a God we could fit inside our heads would not be God. (Isa 55:8–9; Rom 11:33)

label: Faith and reason
title: Watch out
text: Don't apologize for starting with Scripture. Everyone starts somewhere. Don't set faith against thinking. Don't say "you just have to believe." Give a reason. (1 Pet 3:15) Don't think a good argument saves. The problem is not the mind alone, but the heart that suppresses the truth. (Rom 1:18; John 3:19)

label: Faith and reason
title: Bring it to the gospel
text: The most reasonable thing a creature can do is believe his Creator. God has spoken, He has come, and He has raised His Son in proof. (Heb 1:1–2; Acts 17:31) "If God has spoken, is it more reasonable to trust Him or to trust yourself?" Then give The Gospel.

label: For any conversation
title: The fallacy of evolution
text: Why evolution cannot stand, and why creation is true. God made the heavens, the earth and everything in them in six days, and He made man directly, in His image (Gen 1:1; Gen 1:27; Gen 2:7; Ex 20:11). That is our starting point, not our conclusion. Evolution is not a discovery that forced itself on honest observers. It is the origin story of a worldview that has already ruled God out. (Rom 1:20–22; 2 Pet 3:3–6)

label: The fallacy of evolution
title: What you are showing
text: You and he look at the same fossils, the same rocks and the same DNA. The difference is not the evidence. It is the starting point each of you reads it with. No one watched the beginning, and no one can repeat it in a lab. One Witness was there, and He has told us what He did. (Job 38:4; Heb 11:3; Ps 33:6; Ps 33:9) "Were you there? Then whose account of the beginning are you trusting, and why?"

label: The fallacy of evolution
title: The starting point decides the answer
text: Many of evolution's own defenders say so. Harvard geneticist Richard Lewontin wrote that scientists accept material explanations because of a prior commitment to materialism, and that "we cannot allow a Divine Foot in the door" (New York Review of Books, January 9, 1997). That is a rule about what answers are allowed, made before the evidence is looked at. "If God did create, would your method ever be allowed to find that out?"

label: The fallacy of evolution
title: What evolution cannot give you
text: Ask one question at a time and wait for the answer. A beginning. Something does not come from nothing. "Where did matter, energy and the laws they follow come from?" (Gen 1:1; John 1:3) Life. Life has only ever been seen to come from life. Natural selection can only work on something already alive and reproducing, so it cannot explain the first living thing. "How did the first life arise, and has anyone ever seen it happen?" Information. DNA is a code: instructions, stored and read. Everywhere else we find a code, we know a mind wrote it. "Have you ever seen a message write itself?" (Ps 139:13–16) Kinds. We see change within kinds: dog breeds, finch beaks, bacteria that resist a drug. They are still dogs, finches and bacteria. That is variation in what God made "after their kind." It is not one kind turning into another. "Is that change you've watched, or change you've been told happened?" (Gen 1:21; Gen 1:24–25) A mind you can trust. If your brain is the product of survival and not of truth, you have no reason to trust its conclusions, including evolution. Darwin felt this. He wrote of his "horrid doubt" whether the convictions of a mind developed from lower animals "are of any value or at all trustworthy" (letter to William Graham, July 3, 1881). "Why trust a brain that was shaped only to survive?" See Worldviews. Right and wrong. If we are animals shaped by survival of the fittest, there is no "ought."
